speaker: The Chairman
text: Head X, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This year marks SG60 and, on reflection, I believe all in this House will agree that it has been quite an exhilarating and extraordinary journey.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: However, while part of SG60 is to look back and commemorate on our common history and how far we have come, more importantly, it is a time for us to reflect on our shared values and poise ourselves for the road ahead towards a collective future.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our external environment is increasingly volatile and uncertain.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As a small and open nation, the jostling between international powers will have major geopolitical and geoeconomic implications for Singapore and even test us on our nation's social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Domestically, we must continue to be true to our core values, building a caring and inclusive, multiracial, multicultural and multi-religious society.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We want to build a society that is fair, just and able to afford equal opportunities to all Singaporeans to pursue their dreams and aspirations, whatever they may be.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must acknowledge, however, that Singapore, as a society, is rapidly evolving.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We have a rapidly ageing population and a low birth rate.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Technological disruptions have drastically changed our way of life and traditional notions of jobs and the workplace.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must include our youths in these challenging conversations of Singapore in the future as they are the next generation that will inherit Singapore and its policies of today.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: After 60 years of nation-building, if you ask anyone what they take away from Singapore in 2025, you will probably get many different answers.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There will be those who herald our beautiful, green and clean city.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Many will certainly rave about our diverse array of delicious food.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But on this, I must agree with Minister Chan Chun Sing in his hour-long interview with Mothership, it is the "gumption" of Singaporeans that set us apart from everyone else: the "can do, never say die" spirit; the stoic, unbending belief that we will succeed, even with our backs against the wall.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This "gumption" is what got us where we are today.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: And it is this "gumption" that we must preserve if we are to celebrate SG100 together.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: For this to happen, building a strong sense of national unity and identity is crucial.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must ensure that we continue forging and harnessing the unity in purpose and belief in our vibrant and diverse society to keep the flame of our "gumption" burning bright.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: To this end, MCCY plays a vital role in the community building of our society.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share with us MCCY's plans and strategies on how they will expand opportunities in community building as well as the arts, heritage and sports, to build a vibrant and cohesive home that empowers all Singaporeans to excel and achieve their diverse dreams and aspirations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Importantly, how these strategies can help to forge a strong sense of national identity as we build a future together towards SG100.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sharael Taha, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Mr Chairman, various M3 initiatives complement national programmes by strengthening last-mile delivery and customising programmes to be closer to beneficiaries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Volunteers play a crucial role by contributing their skills, knowledge and resources to add value to various initiatives.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: At M3@Pasir Ris-Punggol, the Mari Membaca programme adapts NLB's reading initiative for families with young children, especially in rental blocks.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Jom Sihat programme adapts HPB and MOH programmes to promote healthy lifestyles and health screenings in the community.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Our Learning Journey Visit Programme provides opportunities for youth to understand job roles and industry skills to guide them in career development.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In fact, the Qaryah group at Block 757 Pasir Ris collected $3,000 in just one night.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And tonight, M3@Pasir Ris-Punggol volunteers will also be at the Geylang Serai bazaar to encourage more donations by giving out handmade tokens of appreciation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is evident that M3@Towns can mobilise the community to support various efforts in health, welfare assistance and guidance for children from less privileged backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Good health enables individuals to play active roles in their families and community.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar, you can take your three cuts together.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: MUIS, MENDAKI and Mesra have doubled the impact of their community efforts through close collaboration.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: During the COS debates in 2021, I shared that many in the Malay community did not know what M3 was.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Thankfully, people are becoming increasingly familiar with the name M3, aware of M3 programmes, and an increasing number of people are coming forward to get involved with M3.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Could the Minister share how M3 has laid the foundation for the Malay/Muslim community to become a "Community of Success" and how we can continue to build this momentum for the future? :   Volunteers play a vital role in M3 programmes, serving either as ad hoc volunteers for specific events or through long-term commitments, such as mentoring our youths.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: At the recent launch of the fifth edition of the PEER mentoring programme for secondary school students at M3@Woodlands, I was delighted to meet Umar again.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Umar was a mentee in the first edition of this programme and is now the first mentee to return as a mentor after completing his “A” levels.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Having benefited from this programme, he wants to give back by contributing to the community.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Volunteers should also be empowered with community engagement and leadership skills.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How have we mobilised community assets, including our programme beneficiaries, as volunteers? :   Over the past few years, several M3@Towns have stepped up their efforts to encourage the Malay/Muslim community to take care of their health and practice an active and healthy lifestyle.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I met an 83-year-old resident at the Zumba A Go Go class, thus proving that age is not a barrier to staying active.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: These interest groups also frequently participate in programmes that provide health education and health screenings.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For us at M3, these efforts are highly encouraging.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Could the Minister provide an update on the overall community health outcomes?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In Malay, please. :   Focus Area 5 (FA5) of M3 on Community Health aims to empower our community to take ownership of their health and adopt a sustainable healthy lifestyle.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Minister share what significant improvements we have seen as a result of this FA5?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Has there been a reduced risk of chronic diseases, increase in physical activity, or positive changes in eating habits?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Besides awareness, long-term behavioral changes require community support.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: How does the Government collaborate with mosques, grassroots groups and health professionals to ensure these efforts have a lasting impact?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What are the plans to extend these efforts to harder-to-reach groups, such as the elderly and low-income families?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Many acknowledge that mental health is something they need to address.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: What are the special programmes under M3 that support emotional resilience and mental well-being? :   Sir, strong families are the bedrock of a resilient society.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Government share any update on how Project Dian has improved the well-being of the families involved?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Has there been an increase in employment opportunities, financial stability or community support for these families?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: How does the Government ensure that these families continue to receive the best and holistic support, including financial literacy and parenting guidance, even after they exit the programme?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Due to the challenges of modern life, many in our community now rely on asatizah, not only for religious knowledge but also for guidance in dealing with social and personal issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: How does the Government support asatizah and further empower their role to carry out their duties more effectively?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Are there efforts to provide them with professional training in areas, such as mental health, family counselling and community leadership?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Furthermore, what steps are being taken to ensure that religious institutions and authorities like MUIS continue to provide ongoing support and development to the asatizah, so that they remain relevant and able to meet the community’s needs?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, in Malay. :   Sir, I would like to seek clarification and elaboration on four matters concerning the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: These matters are: (i) the construction and management of mosques; (ii) Warees Halal Limited; (iii) the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS); and (iv) full-time madrasahs.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: My question is, has this percentage remained constant or has it changed?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: And if possible, can the Minister share what is the monthly income of the Mosque Executive Chairman (MEC)?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The website of Warees Halal Limited states that it is a not-for-profit company limited by guarantee, as a subsidiary of MUIS Group whose focus is on providing Halal services and not on generating profits.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Before I continue, I would like to declare that I have a child studying in a full-time madrasah in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: This is highly anticipated by residents of Tampines, Pasir Ris and Punggol.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can we ensure it is easily accessible via public transport, pedestrian paths and cycling routes?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Can the Management Boards of the Istighfar Mosque, Ghufran Mosque, and Al-Islah Mosque be involved so their experience can be utilised in the new mosque's design, including implementing sustainable design for energy efficiency and environmental sustainability? :   Our youths have made significant progress, with more pursuing post-secondary education.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: As they are the future of our nation, we must continue to invest in and empower them to reach their full potential.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Guidance and mentorship are crucial in helping them complete their studies and explore opportunities in growing industries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: At M3@Pasir Ris-Punggol, the mentorship programme run by working youth volunteers has successfully guided at-risk youths, helping them pass examinations and continue their education.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: The Learning Journey programme takes youths to companies across various industries to broaden their mindset towards career opportunities in growing industries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Can the Minister share the outcomes of these efforts and how we can encourage more professionals and companies to support our youth development?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Taha, that will be the last time I give you so much allowance.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Nadia, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Mr Chairman, I am heartened to see the increasing number of opportunities, programmes and initiatives specifically implemented to support our Malay/Muslim youths.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Indeed, many have contributed to help our youths overcome challenges and develop their careers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I refer to the various mentoring programmes that are tailored to help our youths realise their dreams.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These include the #amPowered programme organised by Mendaki, Mara Mentoring by Mendaki Club and Cool-Yah Conversations under M3.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Malay/Muslim organisations also organise many activities to support our youths.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What efforts are being taken to encourage more professionals and organisations to contribute their time in supporting and shaping the next generation?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our Malay/Muslim organisations play an important role in our community.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Now, almost all Malay/Muslim organisations are led by a new generation of leaders.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For our Malay/Muslim youths, such organisations provide opportunities for them to step forward, learn from more experienced community leaders, gain new perspectives beyond the classroom and serve our community and nation.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, how can we empower our Malay/Muslim youths who wish to contribute to society and train themselves to become future leaders?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Has there been any effort to evaluate the effectiveness and impact of these programmes?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Strong and stable families are the foundation that ensures future generations succeed.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some young couples may need support in dealing with fertility challenges or issues they face in their new roles as wives or husbands, or as parents who simply wish to do their best for their children.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, there are various measures and public policies implemented to support our couples and young parents.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the various initiatives introduced by the Government, could the Minister share how these public policies benefit young Malay/Muslim families, especially for parents who have irregular working hours?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, the latest developments of the “Bersamamu” programme.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Early childhood education plays an important role in supporting children's mental development and character formation.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Therefore, may I ask the Minister to share more about the effectiveness of programmes like KelasMateMatika run by Mendaki?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What new programmes are being planned to support our children and young families?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And finally, are there efforts to encourage more young parents to participate in these programmes?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   Research has shown the important role that early childhood education plays in supporting a child’s development for the long-term.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The KelasMateMatika programme for preschoolers is an initiative that seeks to strengthen a child’s basic numeracy skills, while equipping parents with the skills and confidence to facilitate their child’s learning and development.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This initiative is part of the M3 collaboration, which has helped enhance our community's preparedness.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The KMM's long-term impact aligns with MENDAKI's broader goal of improving educational achievement in our community, thus enabling better social mobility.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister share on KMM’s engagement and outreach efforts thus far, and how it has been beneficial for children as well as parents in preparing their children for primary school?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   The Malay/Muslim community has made visible progress in raising its educational level as a whole.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Rapid technological change and constant geopolitical headwinds means new skillsets are required to take on leadership roles across the private, public and people sectors, which is one of the three key pillars defining the Malay/Muslim Community of Success.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How are we supporting Malay/Muslim students amid changes in the education and global economic landscape?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One specific focus area is how we are reviewing the syllabus and teaching methodologies at our madrasahs, which offers an alternative pathway to the national education system that most Singapore students go through.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Education can vary greatly from madrasah to madrasah.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Another area that I am interested in is how our Malay-Muslim self-help groups, like MENDAKI, can play a greater role in amplifying primary and secondary school education.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: KelasMateMatika is a successful and well-cited example of how MENDAKI has successfully supported educational efforts at the early childhood stage.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question to the Minister is, what about beyond that stage?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can we empower our Malay/Muslim students to thrive in new learning environments?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade): Chairman, in Malay, please. :   The economic landscape is rapidly evolving, with technological advancements, automation and industry shifts transforming the nature of jobs and required skill sets.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Emerging sectors such as green technology, digital services and advanced manufacturing present new opportunities, but also require workers to reskill and adapt to remain relevant.

speaker: The Chairman
text: For Malay/Muslim workers, particularly those in vulnerable sectors like traditional retail, F&B and administrative support, there is a growing need to build resilience and equip them with future-ready skills to ensure sustainable career progression.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Could the Minister share insights on how we are ensuring accessibility and effectiveness of these reskilling initiatives for Malay/Muslim workers?

speaker: The Chairman
text: In Singapore’s diverse and multicultural context, it is crucial that our religious leaders are well-equipped to provide guidance to the Muslim community; guidance that is firmly rooted in Islamic scholarship, yet highly attuned to the complexities of their lives.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Specifically, how will the curriculum be designed to ensure that our future asatizah are not only well-versed in traditional Islamic sciences but are also trained to apply their knowledge to contemporary issues, whether it be ethical dilemmas in science and technology, the evolving role of faith in an increasingly secular world or the integration of religious values within a multicultural society like ours?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Beyond local relevance, another key consideration is global engagement.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We know that Singapore has long played a role as a bridge between the East and West, and our asatizah should be similarly prepared to contribute meaningfully to global Islamic discourse.

speaker: The Chairman
text: How will SCIS ensure that its graduates are equipped with the intellectual agility, linguistic proficiency and cross-cultural competencies needed to engage with scholars, policy-makers and communities beyond our shores?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Will there be international partnerships, exchange programmes or collaborative research opportunities that allow our asatizah to gain exposure to diverse schools of thought and global best practices?

speaker: The Chairman
text: SCIS has the potential to be more than just an institution for religious education.

speaker: The Chairman
text: It can be a model for how Islamic scholarship can thrive in a modern, cosmopolitan setting, serving the needs of the local Muslim community and the broader global ummah.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Wakaf plays an important role in the Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Our pioneers have contributed wakaf assets, thus ensuring sustainable financing for mosques, madrasahs and the community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Now, the Wakaf Masyarakat Singapura (WMS) can potentially grow wakaf contributions and enable the community to contribute collectively to charity for the long-term.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Hence, the sustainability of WMS relies on the community’s contributions.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Therefore, as the Chairman of the Islamic Legacy Planning Workgroup, I worked with asatizah, professionals and community partners to raise awareness about the importance of legacy planning since last August's Wakaf Month.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: However, Islamic legacy planning principles and instruments may be difficult to navigate by some segments of the community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: As we make preparations before departing this world, we should also make provisions, not only for our families but also for our community's future through WMS.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Time waits for none; passes each day; Death's hour none can foresee; For the hereafter we make our own way; Through the WMS we help mutually.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Mr Chairman, in Malay, please. :   We celebrate SG60 this year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I am sure many of us are proud of what we have achieved in these 60 years since Singapore became independent, as a multiracial society in the middle of a region with a Malay and Muslim majority.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: We should use SG60 to remind ourselves that we have gotten here because of the contributions of every community.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Moving forward, I think there are at least two areas that our Malay/Muslim community can play an outsized role in the world and shape Singapore’s future on the world stage.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, the SG60 period presents an opportunity for reflection – looking back on how far we have come and renewing our commitment to the shared values that underpin our unity and progress.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past six decades, our Malay/Muslim community has made significant progress, in tandem with the progress of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, my colleagues and I will speak about how we can move forward together as a Community of Success.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, in developing citizenry, we nurture active contributors to community and country; second, in growing competency, where we equip the community for the future while building leaders of tomorrow; and third, in building character, we empower our community and religious sector to progress with confidence.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked how M3 has laid the foundations for a Community of Success.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, we commemorated the fifth anniversary of M3.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Much has been done through the M3's five focus areas, where we identify and address issues in the community, provide more integrated and targeted support to those who most need it and strengthen our last-mile delivery.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These efforts are bolstered by a growing pool of over 4,000 volunteers across the three M3 agencies – MUIS, MENDAKI and the People's Association Malay Activity Executive Committees Council (PA MESRA).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This ethos of active citizenry has been foundational to the work of M3 and in our community and nation building efforts.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I will continue in Malay. :   Chairman, to become active citizens and contribute towards the nation’s development, each individual should remain fit and healthy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We do this by raising awareness on health and providing an environment that encourages a healthy lifestyle among Malay/Muslims.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked for an update on M3 Focus Area 5 (FA5).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Jaga Kesihatan, Jaga Ummah (JKJU) network has also grown, from 100 partners in 2023 to over 160 partners last year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The participants benefitted from JKJU programmes, such as exercise sessions, health talks and healthier groceries distribution.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am pleased to share with Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Mariam Jaafar some positive trends that we observed in the community in recent years.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, the proportion of individuals who have sufficient total physical activity rose from 76% in 2021 to 80% in 2023.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Physical activity here means having at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity per week, including daily routines, such as housework and taking the stairs instead of the lift.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More have also taken part in national programmes like Healthier SG.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, we can do more, such as increasing the proportion of enrolments in the Healthier SG programme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must also intensify efforts to prevent and manage chronic diseases.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The prevalence of diabetes, hypertension and high blood cholesterol in the Malay/Muslim community remains higher than our national average.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Regular health screenings help with early detection and intervention and can prevent or delay the onset of complications of certain diseases.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Health professionals always remind us that the longer we wait to address potential problems, the more complex and costly the treatment can become.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This lags way behind the national average of 63%.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For those aged 40 and above, it is recommended to go for diabetes and high blood cholesterol screening once every three years, and hypertension screening once every two years.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope that the Malay/Muslim community will continue to take charge of their health for the sake of our families, community and country, in order to be active citizens and remain passionate about contributing to Singapore’s development.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Mariam Jaafar asked about M3 efforts to rally community assets and volunteers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2024, the 11 M3@Towns organised over 160 ground-up initiatives, supported by 900 volunteers and benefitting over 65,000 residents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Project Dian is an example of how the Malay/Muslim community works with Government agencies and volunteers to support those living in public rental flats in M3@Towns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Complementing national schemes like ComLink+, Project Dian helps families living in rental flats to improve their stability and income, and work towards helping them purchase and own their flats.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Project Dian started out as a pilot project in three towns in 2021 and now has expanded to six towns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have engaged over 500 households, which represents roughly 70% of the Malay/Muslim families living in rental homes within these towns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Of these families, more than half have young children who have benefitted from additional support that meets their social and educational needs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, the Dian Ambassadors have been matched with families with young children aged three to six years old, to provide support as early as possible, so that these children are better prepared to enter primary school.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The joy is evident on the faces of the children when the Dian Ambassadors read and tell stories to them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope that many more of us will step forward to join this noble cause, and help these families move forward from their current situation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Chairman, Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about Malay/Muslims’ contributions to the SG60 celebrations this year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We launched SG60 Bersama, which organises SG60 celebratory events by the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Members of SG60 Bersama comprises Malay/Muslim organisations, Government agencies and several individuals who came forward to design various programmes for all Singaporeans to enjoy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of these SG60 initiatives is the “60 for 60” Project by PA MESRA.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This initiative exemplifies what it means to pay it forward, where these students will attend a six-month leadership course and learn new skills in areas such as project management and public speaking.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond SG60, the Malay/Muslim community’s efforts in supporting the people of Gaza also demonstrate our show of concern at the global level.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The situation in Gaza remains volatile, and Gaza still needs much help in the areas of humanitarian aid and reconstruction.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The situation is more critical now as they observe their fast in the month of Ramadan.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporeans of all races and faiths have contributed generously towards the provision of critical humanitarian assistance to Gaza.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is a reflection our identity and noble values.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recognise the desire of Singaporeans to do more to help.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Recently, M3 worked with RLAF to launch the Aid for Gaza campaign to raise funds for Gaza.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over Ramadan, volunteers from the M3@Towns will raise funds for Gaza through various ground-up initiatives.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that the theme of the SG60 celebrations “Connect, Care and Contribute” will be further ignited through this campaign.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I look forward to the community’s strong support in together ensuring its success. : Mr Chairman, beyond our shores or closer to home, efforts like M3's Aid for Gaza and our initiatives for local communities in the M3@Towns show how our acts of care and contribution, as donors or volunteers, and how we can connect with one another to do so, can make a difference to those around us.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is what we hope that we can do through the Malay/Muslim community's contribution to the SG60 celebrations or SG60 Bersama.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope this will bring about many opportunities to celebrate our shared culture and heritage and act upon our collective hopes for the future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to contribute to nurture this spirit of citizenry towards the community and towards the country.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is what will propel us forward as a Community of Success in the next 60 years and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, when we look at the progress of our Malay/Muslim community today, there is much that we can be proud of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: About 40 years ago, Malay/Muslim leaders rallied together and founded MENDAKI, when we saw worrying trends in our students' educational performance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many were not completing their Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE), "O" and "A" levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our leaders then recognised the importance of education for the Malay/Muslim community to progress with higher education and better paying jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, we see the impact of the community's self-help efforts through MENDAKI to complement Singapore's education system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To better prepare the community for current and future challenges, MENDAKI has adapted and transformed to stay relevant in raising the competency of the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We approach this with three thrusts: one, expanding MENDAKI's role over the years to address evolving educational needs; two, to better support youths entering the workforce and encourage lifelong learning and upskilling among workers; and three, building community and industry leaders of tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our community has made solid progress, but the work does not stop here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked how we are supporting our students to thrive in new learning environments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI has adapted to new developments in the education landscape while upholding its core mission of student support at every milestone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have made enhancements to the MENDAKI Tuition Programme (MTP), one of the first education initiatives introduced by MENDAKI in the 1980s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I was a beneficiary of the programme then and also volunteered as a tutor when I was in the university.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MTP has also adjusted to changes in the education system, such as Subject-Based Banding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year, MENDAKI will further enhance MTP's programmes by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) systems into our curriculum to better prepare our students for an AI-driven future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will sign memoranda of understanding (MOU) with two institutions which will partner us in this endeavour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, we will work with the Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology Centre (SMART) to provide students with access to AI tools that will help them better grasp Mathematics with topics, such as geometry, and improve the effectiveness of our volunteer tutors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Second, through our partnership with Quantedge Foundation and Temasek Foundation, we will pilot an individualised learning system with diagnostic quizzes and interactive activities, for better student engagement and academic outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI has also moved upstream to invest in preschool education as part of the continuum of support we provide to young families through M3’s Focus Area 1.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is led by Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I agree with Mr Zhulkarnain and Ms Nadia Samdin that preschool builds a strong foundation, not just for academic performance but for holistic development in those crucial years of early childhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Local data has shown that children who attend preschool from age three are less likely to require additional support in primary school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI piloted KelasMateMatika (KMM) in 2018, an early intervention programme, to enhance children's appreciation of numeracy concepts and parents' skills in supporting their children's learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: KMM sets the foundations early for students to perform well in Mathematics, which opens up more educational pathways for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, 90% of students who enrolled in KMM enter primary school without needing additional learning support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the past five years, over 12,000 parents and children have enrolled in KMM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI will continue to work closely with the M3@Towns and social service agencies for even more targeted outreach to young families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Beyond education, MENDAKI has also responded to the professional upskilling needs and to encourage lifelong learning in the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As Mr Fahmi Aliman highlighted, one priority is helping our workers to build resilience and constantly be ready to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This became clear when COVID-19 hit and many workers struggled to keep their jobs in the changing economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, with the rapid technological advancements and innovation, our workers must constantly upgrade and refresh their skills to keep pace with evolving job requirements and secure higher wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To enable more workers to actively upskill and reskill, the Government introduced the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme last year for Singapore Citizens aged 40 and above.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For lower-wage workers, the Workfare Skills Support (Level-Up) will provide a similar monthly training allowance for selected part-time and full-time courses from age 30.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Such programmes provide our workers with opportunities to get a substantial skills reboot and build career resilience, so that they can secure better futures for themselves and their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For Focus Area 4 (FA4) of M3 headed by Mr Fahmi Aliman, it complements national efforts in lifelong learning and helps workers stay competitive as job demands increase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Nadia Samdin asked about the impact of mentoring programmes for our youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI's mentoring programmes, overseen by Minister of State Rahayu Mahzam, aim not only to motivate youths to stay in school but also to raise awareness of career and education opportunities available to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mentoring can help transform perspectives and motivate those from lower-income households, who may not have strong support networks and career role models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Apart from mentoring, our Malay/Muslim professionals have also come together through MENDAKI's Professional Networks to help youths build social capital and open pathways for them to reap the benefits from Singapore's investments in growth sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Of these members, about 60% have actively contributed back through MENDAKI's programmes and ground-up initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, in 2024, the Professional Networks collaborated with MENDAKI to engage close to 650 youths across 17 interactive learning journeys that provided exposure to opportunities in different growth sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Professional Networks in Banking and Finance, Aviation and Technology have also organised networking events for youths to engage professionals on prospective career pathways with these industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI's corporate partners have also come on board to support our youths through scholarships that open doors to job opportunities upon graduation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One example is the Micron Foundation Scholarship and their internship opportunities for polytechnic students pursuing engineering degrees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am glad these efforts have galvanised so many to step forward and I encourage all our professionals to continue reaching out in whatever capacity you can, to make a difference in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin asked about how we are nurturing the next generation of community leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the past, our community leaders contributed their expertise and influence primarily through the Malay/Muslim organisations (MMOs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, many Malay/Muslims are successful across various industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our vision is to draw on all our networks to cultivate leaders of tomorrow who are adept as both community and industry leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To this end, MENDAKI introduced Tunas Bersama M Kuasa Tiga (M3), in 2022 to equip the next generation for leadership roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To widen outreach, MENDAKI has drawn on initiatives such as the Professional Networks to support youths with leadership potential from a broader spectrum of the community and different industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The second cohort of 23 participants includes not just MMO representatives but also M3@Towns Chairpersons and Leads from the Professional Networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The programme allows younger leaders to forge stronger collaborations and exposures, cutting across both community organisations and industry networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, our community has built a strong ecosystem to uplift individuals and prepare for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This would not have happened without those who have persevered through many challenges and steadfastly contributed back.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When he was a student at the Singapore Management University (SMU) in 2004, his family ran into financial difficulties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Firdaus made personal sacrifices so that his younger siblings could continue with school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With support from the Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy (TTFS) and SMU scholarships, he graduated with Magna Cum Laude Honours in 2008.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, Firdaus is a Senior Counsel and regional Head of Legal for a large multinational firm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He also serves on MENDAKI's Education Trust Fund and has joined the second cohort of Tunas Bersama M3.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Firdaus' journey against the odds, inspires us, not just for personal resilience, but also to greater endeavours so we can empower those in similar situations to overcome their challenges and succeed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, I started my speech sharing about MENDAKI's humble beginnings 43 years ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI will keep transforming to better serve the community, whether to expand into preschools, enhancing our mainstream schools' offerings or moving into the workforce to help our workers upskill, reskill and transform to be relevant to the industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the support of our volunteers and partners, we are in a good position to continue progressing as a Community of Success for the future.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, as Singapore marks its 60th year of Independence, it is timely that the Malay/Muslim community reflects on how far we have come and the common aspirations we have as we shape our future together.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our journey has been one of building unity and trust among different communities within our multiracial and multi-religious society, ensuring that we thrive as a Malay/Muslim community and collectively, as a nation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the years, we have been steadfastly pursuing our vision to be a Community of Success, anchored on the three pillars of character, competency and citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: My colleagues spoke about growing competency and exemplifying citizenry in their respective speeches.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our community leaders and volunteers are key in the effort.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together with our M3 agencies and Malay/Muslim organisations, their contributions in bringing people together and for last-mile delivery, have been invaluable in dealing head on with our community's needs, while complementing the Government's efforts at the national level.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will touch on the final "C" – character – which reflects the religious outlook of our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Living in a society marked by change and complexity, our community look to our asatizah for religious guidance.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The quality of asatizah – our Islamic religious teachers and scholars – therefore shapes the character of our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Dr Wan Rizal's query on how our asatizah can meet our community's needs today and in the future, we have stepped up efforts to nurture our asatizah and develop an ecosystem for them to thrive, following recommendations on the Committee on Future Asatizah (COFA) five years ago.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will share three ways we can continue making strides for the asatizah sector: one, grooming the next generation of Singapore Islamic leaders who are equipped to guide the community through contemporary challenges; two, galvanising contributions to strengthen the religious sector and the community; and three, growing the attractiveness of the religious sector.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have been investing in grooming a pipeline of quality asatizah here in Singapore, where they can thrive.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 2020, MUIS introduced the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies (PCICS) to train returning graduates from overseas Islamic universities in the practice of Islam relevant to our context.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Graduates of PCICS shared that they appreciated how the course opened up their worldview.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As importantly, the course also brought them back together again on returning from studying Islam from various overseas universities and uniting them in the process.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Back then, I said the PCICS would lay the foundations for a future Islamic college in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Fahmi Aliman asked about how we have been working to develop the SCIS.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It will offer Islamic teachings, both classical and contemporary, to apply to our context.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Students will be well prepared for employment opportunities in the religious and adjacent sectors.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through these programmes, students can gain practical skills to better contribute to different facets of socio-religious life in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For those interested in pursuing their post-graduate studies after SCIS, MUIS is working with our foreign partner institutions to enable interested students to benefit from advanced standing for postgraduate programmes at these institutions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These opportunities are possible because of our partnerships with local and foreign institutions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These distinguished partners are a testament to how our vision to establish SCIS is held in high regard and resonates internationally.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through partnering world-class Islamic institutions, we can also ensure the SCIS is globally relevant, while remaining responsive to Singapore's context.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have put in place an Advisory Panel, a Steering Committee and a Board of Governors to guide SCIS' development.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Steering Committee, led by Mufti Dr Nazirudin, has started the important work of charting the roadmap for the SCIS' developments.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Board of Governors, chaired by Mr Abdullah Tarmugi, will play a key role in stewarding the College's governance and providing oversight on matters like fees and entry qualifications.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For more information on our journey to develop the SCIS thus far, I invite Members to collect a copy of the SCIS booklet, "Building the Foundations", from the Parliament Library.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, in Malay, please. :   Chairman, the SCIS reflects our ongoing efforts to meet the socio-religious needs of our Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our mosques have also been a key node for the Malay/Muslim community’s religious life.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Faisal Manap asked about mosque development plans.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The mosque in Tampines North was announced in 2015.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the time, the area was still under development.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 2019, we upgraded Masjid Darul Ghufran with a larger prayer hall to accommodate more congregants.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The construction of the mosque in Tampines North was delayed due to COVID-19, which also significantly impacted the implementation of other planned infrastructure projects.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When the situation improved, MUIS reviewed the mosque development plans and decided that planning for new mosques could proceed.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS works closely with national agencies on the planning of new mosques, which considers demographic changes and population projections with the development of new towns across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Mr Faisal Manap’s query, there are currently 32 mosques under the management of Executive Chairmen while the rest are led by Honorary Chairmen.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our Executive Chairmen receive competitive compensation packages that commensurate with their responsibilities in managing mosque operations and serving the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Faisal Manap also asked about Warees Halal Limited (WHL).

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: WHL was set up to provide a complementary role to MUIS’ Halal Certification Unit.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given significant developments in the halal regulatory regime and the halal industry over the years, MUIS will continue to review the role of WHL in response to these changes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Back to Mr Faisal Manap’s question on the sharing of costs to pay for the employment of Mosque Executive Chairmen, the cost-sharing arrangement between MUIS and the mosques is reviewed based on the mosques' financial capabilities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even as we ensure we have enough funds to build new mosques and to establish the SCIS, we must also ensure that our community’s funds are sustainable.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, the Wakaf Masyarakat Singapura (WMS), which was launched last year to support the long-term religious needs of the Malay/Muslim community, is crucial.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: WMS will create a long-term, sustainable funding stream for our community and empower the Malay/Muslim community to chart a brighter future.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS set up the WMS Protem Committee to establish strong foundations for the governance and implementation of WMS.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked how we can help our community better understand Islamic legacy planning principles and instruments.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To achieve this aim, MUIS formed the Islamic Legacy Planning Workgroup (ILPW) comprising lawyers, financial planners and estate planners, as well as asatizah.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Out of this amount, almost $1 million are cash contributions, and the remainder in pledges.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is five times the number of about 1,150 pledgers currently.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I hope more among us will contribute to WMS.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our contributions will go a long way in supporting the socio-religious needs of our future generations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, our asatizah contribute beyond their traditional role of religious instruction.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They also support the community in other ways.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Nadia Samdin, who asked for an update on Bersamamu, may be glad to know that our Kadi and Naib Kadi have journeyed with about 31,000 couples so far.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They are competent in other areas like marriage counselling or as Marital First Responders, family violence awareness and financial literacy.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Therefore, they are well-informed of the trends and issues of married couples, and are more equipped to guide these couples.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Bersamamu is part of the community support ecosystem, complementing national-level initiatives that we have in place for young couples and families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In response to Ms Nadia Samdin, we can do more to help young families who face additional challenges.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Prime Minister has announced a suite of Budget initiatives to support growing families and in early childhood care and education, which we hope will benefit many Malay/Muslim families as well.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ongoing initiatives like KidSTART also equip parents with the knowledge and skills to confidently support their child’s development.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I encourage the selected families to join KidSTART through touchpoints like ComLink+ as well as Bersamamu.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Just like how our Kadi and Naib Kadi provide invaluable support to families, we see the same spirit in FITRAH’s asatizah volunteers, where 40 asatizah from 29 mosques have stepped forward beyond their roles as Mosque Religious Officers (MROs) to support various services offered by FITRAH.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our asatizah also play a key role in forging trust and mutual understanding between different faiths and communities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They lead their congregants to continue to actively expand our common spaces and open the mosques to other communities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is especially felt during this Ramadan, when the mosques welcome non-Muslim friends to join us for “buka puasa”, as we share the joy and blessings of Ramadan together.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must therefore ensure that the religious sector remains attractive to have a steady pipeline of quality asatizah.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: On average, the madrasahs accept one of every two students who apply.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS has conducted rigorous evaluations of the asatizah’s job scope, benchmarked their salaries against related sectors at the national level and engaged employers to ensure that salary adjustments are competitive and sustainable.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS is committed to working with employers to continue adjusting our asatizah’s salaries so that it commensurates with their knowledge and skills.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is also done so that they meet the national salary benchmarks for relevant sectors progressively.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We hope that these moves will provide assurance for our asatizah and recognise all their hard work in providing religious guidance and pastoral support for the Muslim community – that even in their chosen career, they can provide a comfortable living for themselves and their families, just like every other Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In English): Through our shared commitment and collective efforts, our vision of a Community of Success is not just a model that resonates within Singapore – it is now recognised and respected beyond our shores.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I look forward to sharing more about our plans in my speech at my annual Hari Raya Get-Together in April.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, as we celebrate SG60, we stand on the firm foundation of our community’s strong religious Character, which continues to guide us as we grow in Competency and nurture a deep sense of Citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Character keeps us united, competency will make us strong and citizenry, trusted.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These pillars will propel us forward, uniting us in purpose and progress.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, as a Community of Success, we will shape a brighter future for our community and for Singapore.

speaker: The Chairman

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I have two areas of clarifications: one for Senior Minister of State Zaqy and another for Minister.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: For Senior Minister of State Zaqy, two questions.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: First on KMM, whether MENDAKI can look into plans to expand KMM beyond Mathematics and, possibly, into science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), for example?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Second, how is MENDAKI following through with the various graduated cohorts of KMM batches to track their educational outcomes in primary school?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: For the hon Minister, on WMS and legacy planning.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: First question: what are the efforts that MUIS is undertaking with the other national agencies to streamline resources or share resources for the purposes of promoting legacy planning, like making wills, CPF nominations and insurance nominations?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Second, our Malay/Muslim community may have various conventional investments or insurance policies that may not be strictly Shariah-compliant in the conventional funds.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Will there be further religious guidance from the Office of the Mufti in this regard?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I will take the question in two parts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At preschools, we have beyond the KMM programme, STEM programme as well for preschoolers and their parents at Raikan Ilmu at Heartlands as an example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We give them exposure to playing with robots, toys and other ways in which to explore more experientially rather than typical tuition or academic formats.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We also have Instagram platforms to engage parents as well to give them courses, classes and exposure to the developmental programmes that they can take kids through with STEM.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the data and studies level, those are just as important because that informs us on the effectiveness of the KMM programme.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it has been quite effective in that sense and we continue to monitor it, especially when we scale.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And one of the key factors is really how we engage parents and the parents in cultivating that love and interest in Mathematics.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That makes a difference for many of our preschoolers who may have underperformed or may not have been able to clear LSM in the past but today, are with current cohorts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And certainly, with our MTP, our kids who graduate from KMM are automatically enrolled in MTP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That helps us ensure that we continue to have touchpoints so that while they have gained the knowledge and benefits in Primary 1, they do not lose it and we continue to track them when they enter mainstream school.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To the question from Mr Zhulkarnain, we are very glad that other agencies in the Government are very keen to support us and to help us in the growing of the funds for WMS.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For the Malay/Muslim community, the reliance on instruments like faraid, where one's estate will be automatically distributed after their passing on, is a tradition we have had for the longest time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But actually, the real tradition in the Islamic practice is to have a will, always to have a will.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And that is a practice that we have not practised in this part of the world, because we assume the Government or MUIS will take care of whatever we leave behind.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The will is a very important instrument, not only for WMS, but for people we want to give to, who may not benefit from the faraid distribution.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we hope that this awareness of WMS also creates awareness of the need to always have a will.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just a practice I would like to share with Members here is that, in the early days of Islam, everyone in the adherents of Islam had a will.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To the fact that when they leave home to travel or when they went to war in those days, they would look back at the will and see whether the people they left this will behind for were still alive or if it should be changed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, the distribution of the estate is the will first, and then debts and, then faraid.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, faraid is the default, but only when you do not have a will or you have cleared your debts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, this instrument is a very important instrument and through WMS, we would like them to be aware that they should really have a will, and also, while doing a will, leave something for WMS.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: But due to time factors, I will submit a Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, can I seek a clarification from the Minister whether does he MUIS to work with the full-time madrasahs to increase the number of Primary 1 places in these full-time madrasahs?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Before I respond to the questions, I would like to ask Mr Faisal Manap whether he wants us to expand or he is asking me whether we should expand the places in the madrasahs.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Just asking whether MUIS can work with the full-time madrasahs to expand the number of intakes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Chairman, when we receive or accept the placement into the madrasah, we are not just looking at the point of entry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to look at the whole journey the child will take and we are responsible for it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That means that by the time they leave school, they must have a livelihood; and this is the reality of living in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is not just pursuing an education to fulfil the dreams of the parents alone, but we must be able to ensure that when they go out, they have a career, a meaningful career and livelihood.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, for those 400, those who cannot continue, they are able to continue their national stream with no problems, which is why we do not have any dropouts in that sense of the word.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And for this 150 who move on to become asatizahs, we want to ensure that they are competent, and when they come back, they have a job waiting for them, they have a livelihood that they can rely on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But then, again, it is focused on the interest of the community's needs, as well as to ensure that every child that gets into our madrasah system does not lose out in becoming a contributing citizen in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I have one other question to answer which is the mosque executive chairmen.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But today, what we have looked at is the ability of the mosque and how much fund they can collect on a monthly basis, and then a portion, according to their affordability.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are also a mix of legislation, policies, unique commemorative events and education in school and for the public, through campaigns to strengthen racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The National Education lessons and current issues discussions are also aimed at nurturing in our young the notion that this social compact is significant and can only be preserved through deep commitment and belief in racial and religious harmony and inclusivity at all levels of society.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many public campaigns also aim at fostering respect and instilling understanding of the importance of being open, respectful and culturally aware.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: It will also provide a significant boost to the arts sector economy.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Usha Chandradas, please take your four cuts together.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, the CMF matches donations but not the earned income of registered arts charities.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I have heard from some arts charities that this makes fundraising events, like the throwing of gala dinners actually much more "lucrative" than pitching for work or projects.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The irony here is that if charities were out in the field securing contracts and paid work, as some charities do, they would be creating a multiplier effect, generating freelance and subcontracting opportunities down the line for other workers and players in the arts.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: If we expect arts and heritage charities to be self-sustaining to an extent – and not to rely entirely on donations – why not support them more when they take steps to earn their own revenue?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: CMF backing for earned income would not be out of step with the broader mission of arts charities, it would actually reward sustainability and encourage charities to innovate in finding new revenue streams.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: These could include fees for advice on compliance, contracts or intellectual property matters.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
