text: These are essential operational costs that ensure charities remain accountable and that they are legally protected.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Excluding them potentially undermines charities' ability to function effectively and sends the implicit message that these kinds of costs are not "necessary" operational costs.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Third, the non-profit sector struggles to attract and retain skilled talent, yet the CMF matching grants cannot be used for staff bonuses or welfare benefits.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: If we want to professionalise the arts charity sector, we must acknowledge that talent retention is just as crucial as the direct funding of artistic programmes.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: There is a long-standing misconception that non-profit staff are less valuable in some way than their private or public sector counterparts.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Excluding staff bonuses and welfare costs from CMF matching support potentially reinforces this bias too.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: It could have the effect of undermining our efforts to build a strong, motivated workforce within the arts and heritage charity sector.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The CMF is an extremely meaningful initiative, I do not deny this – all I am saying is that the exclusions for the usage of the matching grants, in themselves, send a message about how we view charities' human resources and their legal and compliance obligations.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I acknowledge and am grateful for MCCY's ongoing support for Chinese and minority cultural arts groups, but these groups continue to face challenges.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Minority arts groups represent smaller communities and can struggle to gain visibility, especially if their content is not delivered in English.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, arts groups offering Chinese language- or Chinese traditional performances can find it difficult to attract younger audiences and new patrons.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Both sets of groups have also shared with me that mainstream philanthropic networks are harder for them to access, making it sometimes difficult for them to fund raise.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, the arts have a unique power to transcend cultural boundaries.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: They can foster emotional connections between different communities and, in so doing, strengthen racial harmony.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: MCCY should encourage crossover audiences in arts events – that is to say, bringing Chinese audiences to non-Chinese arts performances and offerings, and vice versa.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The work of minority and non-English arts groups is about more than just cultural preservation, it strengthens social cohesion as well.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: When I spoke to Dr Kasinathan, who was a long-term secretary and now patron at the Singapore Indian Fine Arts Society (SIFAS) – which coincidentally celebrated its 75th anniversary this past weekend – I asked him what, to him, was one of the most significant achievements of SIFAS?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Dr Kasi told me that he was proud that the organisation "not only created opportunities for students of all races to learn and participate in the Indian fine arts, but that bursaries if required were also equally available." I have also personally seen the impact of cross-cultural engagement firsthand, at the theatre.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: At AGAM Theatre Lab's "Tharuthalai Thirutham", I saw audiences of different backgrounds moved to tears by the storytelling, even though not everyone understood Tamil.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: When watching Nine Years' Theatre's "See You, Anniversary," delivered entirely in Chinese, which is a language I barely understand, I was deeply moved.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: These experiences show that language is no barrier to emotional connection.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Art has the power to create bonds that go well beyond theoretical slogans about racial harmony.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: To support cross-cultural engagement in the arts, I propose three suggestions.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: This could include collaborations with mainstream media, influencers or targeted digital campaigns.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Second, could MCCY act as a bridge between these arts groups and philanthropists?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: These groups could lack direct access to new patrons and facilitating introductions through things like private showcases, receptions or dialogue sessions could help them to connect with new potential patrons or supporters.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Third, could MCCY introduce a new recognition platform for philanthropists who support artistic projects that bridge different racial and ethnic communities?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: At present, the Patron of the Arts Award broadly differentiates donors by the monetary value of their contributions.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps, we could consider a new category of awards, a Cultural Visionary Patron Award, for example, for philanthropists who support arts groups which bridge diverse cultural expressions and accordingly promote racial harmony through the arts.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: However, as with any new advancement, opportunities will come with risks and challenges.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Christie’s, for example, just concluded its first sale of AI-generated art.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The artistic community had a mixed response, with some raising concerns over AI’s use of copyrighted works while others embraced its creative potential.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: We can see that the intersection of art and technology is not just a space for experimentation but also a potential economic driver.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: That being said, in Singapore, many artists still lack access to the necessary tools or training to integrate emerging technologies into their work.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Others may be wary of venturing into unfamiliar territory.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: It may be too expensive to attend courses to acquire these skills, and there may be concerns over ethical and legal issues.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Many artists remain concerned about issues, such as that of artwork ownership rights, intellectual property protection and fair compensation for digital creations.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond access to tools and training, will there be initiatives to educate artists on how to protect their intellectual property rights in the digital realm?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: On a related note, does MCCY have any plans to use technology to engage younger audiences and deepen their appreciation for the arts?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: With digital platforms playing an increasingly central role in how content is consumed, innovative approaches, such as interactive virtual exhibitions, AI-assisted creative tools or gamified experiences, could especially help to bridge the gaps between traditional art forms and younger generations.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: And I would appreciate any insight the Minister might have on how MCCY has been thinking about these opportunities.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I fully agree with the Minister that the development of a competitive and sustainable arts sector is key, but I want to emphasise that salary guidelines are not a distraction from this goal.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: They are, in fact, a meaningful component of it.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I have spoken to many young artists and aspiring arts workers who feel anxious about entering the job market because they have no clear expectations of pay, especially if they seek to be freelancers.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Anecdotally, you still hear stories of exploitation where people, especially younger workers, are asked to work for free or without proper pay.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Without transparent guidelines, both workers and employers struggle to navigate fair compensation.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: This can lead to inconsistencies that will affect the sector’s ability to attract and retain talent.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: With this in mind, I offer three targeted suggestions for MCCY’s consideration.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: First, could MCCY examine the precedent that has been set by the National Council of Social Service (NCSS)?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: These are issues that are also relevant to the arts.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: While it may be too early to assess the full impact of the NCSS model, could MCCY consider whether a similar approach could be adapted for the arts sector to provide clearer pay benchmarks and career progression pathways?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Second, could MCCY help to address the lack of salary benchmarking in the arts sector?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Many arts organisations struggle to set salaries and remuneration due to a lack of publicly available data, especially for freelancers.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: While some financial information on Institutions of Public Character (IPCs) is available on the Charities Portal, it lacks detailed data on compensation and this makes it difficult even for well-intentioned employers to structure fair wages competitively.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: There are arts administrators, economists and industry analysts who can provide valuable insights if given access to relevant data and market players.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: A study could also directly engage arts workers, ensuring that any proposed guidelines, if they are issued, will reflect real market conditions and concerns.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I hope the Minister will consider these proposals and I welcome further discussion on this point.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Some shared that freelance work could increase feelings of isolation and loneliness.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Could MCCY provide an update on its efforts under the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy in respect of freelancers?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Could MCCY share how it is working with Government procuring agencies and stakeholders to improve the mental health and well-being of freelance coaches, instructors and creators?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: For instance, the stART Fund that supports traditional Chinese arts and emerging Chinese visual artists and calligraphists.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Some of these schemes are also customised for the artists’ needs.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: There are also campaigns like The Esplanade's Arts for Change campaign, which aims to make arts more accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: While the Government has invested in the arts scene, there might be a perception that the arts are not as valued as other industries.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: There are limited performance spaces, difficulties in making a decent living from the arts alone and perhaps a greater need for audience engagement and appreciation for artistic talent.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Can MCCY share the plans to strengthen and support artists to develop their talent and skill to realise their full potential?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Could MCCY share its plans to strengthen support for artists, particularly in developing their talents and skills so they can realise their full creative potential and sustain long-term careers in the arts?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: To provide for housing and industrial needs, many historical buildings were torn down.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: But the Government ultimately recognised that our buildings are a critical part of our heritage and the need to preserve for future generations.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Heritage building preservation led by the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) through its conservation programmes focuses on maintaining the original character, and historical and architectural significance of these buildings while allowing for modern functionality.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Singapore encourages repurposing old buildings for new purposes, like retail spaces, restaurants and cultural centres, while preserving the features of the buildings.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Some of these buildings are not just iconic but a part of the Singapore story, significant for our collective cultural memory.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Some notable examples of repurposed heritage buildings are CHIJMES, formerly the Convent of the Holy Infant Jesus School downtown, which is repurposed into a mixed-use development with restaurants, shops and event spaces.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The Old Police Academy along Thomson Road is now a contemporary art centre.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The Singapore Art Museum has moved to Tanjong Pagar Distripark and is doing well in attracting new audiences in this space.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Golden Mile Complex, an example of Brutalist architecture, slated for redevelopment into The Golden Mile, a conservation development including offices, medical suites and lifestyle spaces.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: These preservation initiatives maintain Singapore’s rich national culture while supporting urban development.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Singapore’s rich multicultural heritage is a vital part of our national identity and should be accessible, celebrated and preserved for future generations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: From our historical districts to traditional trades, our cultural heritage reflects the shared experiences and contributions of our diverse communities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: However, sustaining interest and deepening appreciation requires proactive efforts to engage Singaporeans, especially our younger generation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Can the Minister share what can be done to ensure that the community continues to sustain interest in, and deepen appreciation for, our cultural heritage?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And beyond cultural sites and festivals, heritage businesses also play an important role to shape our identity, serving communities for decades with high-quality products and services that have stood the test of time.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Many of these businesses are not just commercial enterprises but keepers of traditional crafts, recipes and experiences that define Singapore’s unique character.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For example, in Kebun Bahru, we have the largest remaining bird singing club left in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And next to the club, there are one or two little shops with a couple of craftsmen who do handcrafted and handmade bird cages.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: They may not generate a lot of sales but their presence shaped the look and feel of the surrounding bird-singing community.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Yet, as we have seen in recent cases in Marine Parade, these long-established businesses face challenges, including rising rentals, changing consumer habits and competition from large retail chains.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: While urban renewal and commercial viability are important, it is equally critical that we find ways to safeguard and support heritage businesses so that Singapore does not lose these cultural icons.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Can the Minister share any plans to recognise and support our heritage businesses, ensuring they remain a meaningful part of Singapore’s cultural and economic landscapes for years to come?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Hany Soh, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Even so, many Woodgrove residents have told me that there are more places in our division that also deserve a spotlight.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For years, residents have wondered why a neighbourhood park in Woodgrove carries this name when we are nowhere near Mandai or Tekong.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I recently learned from a senior resident that the park was likely named after a former village off Mandai Road.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: During HDB’s Rejuvenation of Heartlands project recently, this park got a major facelift, reflecting the kampung spirit with its play features.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It was formerly known as Hock Chun Community Centre.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Following Senior Minister Lee’s visit to Marsiling in 2019, he shared through his social media that Hock Chun Community Centre was Singapore’s first rural community centre.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: He had actually attended its opening with our founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew back in 1963.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Although the present-day Fuchun Community Centre is no longer located at its original site, such valuable history must be passed down to the next generation and generations to follow.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, this year marks SG60 and here in Woodgrove, we are excited to welcome our newly renovated Fuchun Community Centre, complete with green sustainability features and amenities for both young and old to bond as a community and family.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I hope the NHB will seriously consider updating the Woodlands Heritage Trail to include a new trail marker at this Community Centre when it reopens in the second quarter of this year, to let this kampung spirit, that has evolved since 1963, to continue to pass down for generations.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Every Singaporean child deserves a chance to explore the arts.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is how they discover creativity, appreciate their culture and see the world in new ways.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The National Arts Council's Arts Education Programs serve this purpose by providing students access to quality arts education experiences that complement curriculum and co-curriculum learning.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On this note, how can MCCY do even more, to expose our young to the arts?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can this initiative be expanded to also benefit younger children in preschools?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A similar family-focused design like the Active SG credits for the SG Culture Pass could help instill a love to the arts from an early age, while enhancing family bonding.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If lowering the age is not possible, I would urge the Ministry to team up with vendors to offer waivers or reduced fees for kids who come with adults.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Or as another option, let these children use their Life SG credits to cover these costs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I congratulate Yeo Jia Min and Loh Kean Yew on their stellar performance in the recent German Open Badminton tournament.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They and other team Singapore athletes have blazed a trail for many more athletes to follow.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The level of competition in world-class sport is fierce, with elite athletes dedicating their youth to training and competing.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Winning at the highest level requires early talent identification, top-tier coaching and strong athlete support.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These student athletes take a different path from their peers in mainstream schools.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Training 20 hours to 30 hours a week and travelling frequently for competitions while studying, is extremely demanding.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Not all can enrol in a Singapore Sports School, because its 10 academy programmes may not match the athlete's sport.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: SportSG and National Sports Associations (NSAs) must work more closely with mainstream schools, therefore, to give student athletes greater flexibility in their schedules, while ensuring they keep up academically.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Finances are a major hurdle to developing world-class athletes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Most costs, especially in the early years, fall on parents.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Without external funding, we risk limiting our talent pool to the wealthiest households.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Funding need not come solely from the Government.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: SportSG and NSA should play a bigger role in securing and connecting athletes with sponsorship opportunities.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Even modest sponsorship of equipment, clothing or travel, can help to develop potential talent.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Young athletes and their parents need clearer guidance and structured pathways, so they do not navigate the system alone.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: More support should be provided to help parents make informed decisions about their child's sporting and academic future.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In such cases, SportSG should provide more guidance and oversight to support athletes and help them to achieve their full potential.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: World-class athletes are developed through years of rigorous training, not talent alone.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If we are serious about competing on a world stage, we must put in the right structures, pathways and financing in place for our athletes to train, develop and win.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The web-based platform was meant to address the problems faced by users in booking sport facilities.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I seek an update on whether these dealing issues have been ironed out.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: On a more concerning note, there was a commentary carried by CNA in November 2024 on the appearance of badminton groups organising games in exchange for a fee from participants.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Individuals interviewed for the piece expressed their unhappiness over having to pay the host who organised badminton games, but at the same time will also resign to the realities that these groups leveraged on their members to secure slots at facilities, something that is more difficult for an individual on their own.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I urge MCCY, SportSG and stakeholders to look into improving the booking process further.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Under the previous “first-come first-served” system, if residents were unsuccessful in securing a booking, they would know immediately and could quickly look for alternative venues.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Now, they have to wait for the ballot result with each booking attempt, taking more than 24 hours.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Some residents would prefer a system that provides immediate result. : Madam, second, we should not allow individuals who secure ActiveSG court bookings to host strangers and organise games for a fee.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: While this practice is not outright "on-selling", it is effectively "fractional on-selling", masquerading as the hosting and convening.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I am not against private players creating a market to convene strangers to play sports together, but do this on private courts.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: We should not allow the hosting of games for a fee on public courts funded by taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I urge ActiveSG to step up efforts to detect and weed out this practice.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Be a "mystery shopper", join these hosted sessions and gather direct evidence of what is going on.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Or better yet, ActiveSG itself can step into the market and host groups on public courts.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Emulate private market practices, do it ourselves on public courts for the public good.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: One way in which the Government has been encouraging a healthy lifestyle, is by the provision of the ActiveSG credits.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, I would like to ask whether there are any new or upcoming programmes planned for 2025 that will complement this top-up, ensuring that everyone in Singapore is motivated and supported to fully leverage the facilities and programmes available.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In the meantime, the Sports Hub continues its work in developing sporting and lifestyle offerings for Singaporeans and support the development of sporting excellence of our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It binds us and it drives us forward as one people.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At MCCY, we serve as the custodians of this spirit; nurturing our nation's heart and soul, transforming Singapore from a city into a home – one where everyone, regardless of their background, can contribute to our shared story.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Whether it is in the arts, heritage or culture, or in sport, music or religion – these are all strands of the Singapore spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Collectively, they make up the Singapore identity – one that is richly woven into a multi-ethnic tapestry.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The challenges ahead – both internal and external – will be daunting; which is why we think that now, more than ever, we need to nurture and strengthen the Singapore spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At MCCY, we will double down on our efforts to serve Singaporeans and build a society that can stand united and strong, embodying "We, the people of Singapore", enabling our diverse aspirations to shine and building our shared future, together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They have given us much to think about by way of ideas and suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleagues and I will respond to as many as possible in our speeches.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the years, we have built a strong united nation founded on key values, like resilience, openness and self-determination.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Mr Darryl David said, "SG60 is an opportunity to reflect on our past." We agree. "We should celebrate our shared values and prepare for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our pioneers embodied these values and etched them into our national fabric." Indeed, we should document and celebrate the stories of these pioneers, to preserve the values that make Singapore, well, uniquely Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our shared values, as well as our collective experiences – these are what bind us together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have witnessed this in so many moments that we have had.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am sure many of the Members here will have their own account, but just last year, we saw religious leaders coming together, engaging in a historic interfaith dialogue with the Pope, or our residents enjoying arts in their own heartlands, as some of you have spoken about, through our programme, ArtsEverywhere@CDC or athletes surpassing themselves at the Paris Olympics and Paralympics and the many school and community events at the Sports Hub, which have brought people together and many more.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These, and other shared moments are the foundation of our identity as "We, the people of Singapore".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In our highs, we celebrate together; in our lows, we support each other.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At MCCY, we will build on them and we will remain committed to creating opportunities and occasions for more Singaporeans to come together to experience such moments.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are progressing on our plans to add other gyms and sports centres around Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also reimagined the Disability Sports Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To increase accessibility and awareness of our disability sport programmes and activities, not only for the disability community, but also for the broader public – to drive greater awareness, as well as stronger inclusion.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to reduce barriers and create more incentives to drive greater participation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We hope this will further encourage sport participation across more community segments.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Neil Parekh, who just spoke a moment ago, will be glad to know that previous instances of credit top-ups that took place in 2014 and more recently, in 2023, were positively received, with about two in three ActiveSG Members using the credits within a year of the top-up and the announcement.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With this SG60 top-up, we hope that we can push on, to enhance mass sports participation, so that all Singaporeans can live better through sport.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Culture Pass is an integral part of our Arts Plan 2.0, aiming to foster a deeper connection and appreciation between the Singapore audience and the arts and heritage in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, this programme also seeks to strengthen the support for our own local practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To Mr Sitoh Yih Pin's question, it is my hope that this will ignite a passion for more arts appreciation amongst Singaporeans and inculcate in as many Singaporeans as possible, a lifelong interest in the arts and a deeper appreciation in their own heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She had also raised several queries during the Budget debate and earlier when she spoke.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling will address the other queries that the Member has raised.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I said, our aim is for the Culture Pass to impact as many Singaporeans as possible, especially those who have not attended or do not usually attend local arts and heritage events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But they can be used to purchase tickets for family and friends so that they can go together and enjoy the programmes together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is because younger audiences will be able to benefit from arts education and outreach programmes that are embedded into schools, which NAC supports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Parents will be able to use their credits, however, to bring their children along for local arts and culture events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We hope that, overall, this can encourage Singaporeans to come together to engage in a shared experience of our local arts and culture.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, Madam, is also why we focus on in-person experiences for the Culture Pass, rather than virtual experiences or purchases of artworks or art materials.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In-person activities create opportunities for all Singaporeans to come together and create a community around art appreciation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That said, we recognise that in some cases, for example, in the literary arts, the primary mode of appreciation is through the written word, through books.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let me reassure Ms Usha Chandradas that we will continue to ensure that diverse groups of all sizes will have fair access to the programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will pull all eligible offerings onto a single website, which will help publicise events from different groups.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And this helps the smaller groups who might not be able to afford the resources to publicise, gain additional mindshare and publicity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There are some understandable concerns that some parties may take the opportunity to profiteer.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But I believe that with the wide array and variety of programmes to choose from, it suits basically everyone, whoever has a local offering, in arts and culture and heritage, will be on the programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We think that arts groups will be incentivised to price their offerings competitively, reflecting their true value.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But at the same time, having said that, we will also continue to monitor and review the effectiveness of the scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we had a dialogue with the arts and heritage community and we have therefore come up with our Culture Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is in a form that I think is workable, but we will continue to take feedback from users on its implementation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Alongside the SG60 ActiveSG credit top-up and the SG Culture Pass, we will also have a busy and bustling calendar of events to bring Singaporeans together over shared experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In October, the Singapore Biennale 2025 will bring art outside of traditional museum spaces and into the public realm.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin can be assured to know that we will be leaning forward to provide a diverse portfolio of events at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At that time, we made a commitment to bring in more community and sporting events, and to transform the Sports Hub into a vibrant space that all Singaporeans can enjoy and identify with.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since then, we have fulfilled this and done much more.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We saw an all-time high in the number of National School Games Finals held at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have hosted a range of sporting and community events that we never had before at the Sports Hub, such as the Let's Celebrate 2025 New Year Countdown, HYROX, Harmony Fest, and the Singapore Tennis Open, to name a few of the recent ones.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also brought in top-tier global artistes, both western and eastern, into Singapore, for multi-night concerts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And Members might know, we just announced this morning that Lady Gaga will be performing at the Sports Hub for a few nights in May.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Kallang Alive Sports Management team has worked hard and worked innovatively to bring such events into Singapore, and we will continue to hustle and bring in the best events across sport, entertainment and lifestyle to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have reclaimed the Sports Hub as a place for all Singaporeans and will continue to do so with the Kallang Alive Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On the Masterplan, Members might recall that the Kallang Alive Masterplan was first announced by Prime Minister at last year's National Day Rally.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As part of this plan, we will also be developing a new indoor arena and have precinct enhancements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will enable us to host more sporting, lifestyle and entertainment events, and also increase the vibrancy of the precinct with community sporting facilities and programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These developments will complement our plans for the home of Team Singapore, a topic of which I will return later in my speech.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, Madam, we will continue to open up more pathways for Singaporeans to chart their own successes and reach their own full potential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the arts, we now have a vibrant ecosystem of world class, creative and dedicated practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would regard them as being amongst the best globally.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This success stems from years of careful planning and investment in our arts community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through strategic initiatives like the Arts and Culture Strategic Review and Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans, we have set up clear, multiyear plans with strong foundations and have also taken a special care to nurture talent at every level.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have established institutions, like the School of the Arts and more recently, the University of the Arts Singapore (UAS) to shape the next generation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We provide career resources and on-the-job training through platforms, such as the NAC's Arts Resource Hub, particularly for the many freelancers who contribute so much and thrive in the arts community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, we are proud to have world-class institutions like the National Gallery and the Singapore Art Museum for visual arts, The Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay for performing arts, and the National Museum of Singapore and Asian Civilisations Museum, amongst others, for heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But Madam, there is one area where we see untapped potential and that is in the area of design.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have after all been a UNESCO Creative City of Design since 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our people-centric urban design is renowned around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our designers have gained international acclaim, with many working at the highest levels around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, in the realm of fashion, we have Andrew Gn, who is based in Paris but very well-known internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He will be exhibiting in the US later this year, the first retrospective of a Singaporean designer overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, Singapore-based jewellery brand State Property Fine Jewellery, founded by Afzal Imram as well as Lin Ruiyin, has been worn by the likes of Lady Gaga and Michelle Obama.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the realm of architecture, Kampong Admiralty, designed by homegrown architecture firm WOHA, won World Architecture Festival's World Building of the Year in 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And in industrial design, Hans Tan's works have been collected by major international museums, such as M+ in Hong Kong and Cooper Hewitt in New York.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We already have strong programmes to groom the next generation of design talents, such as those at UAS, which include cutting-edge programmes, such as Biophilic Design and Design for Social Futures.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We should showcase and promote their talents even more.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But let me also add that design is not just about aesthetics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Good design makes our lives better, can be a key driver of innovation, value creation and international branding for Singapore businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This museum could showcase the best of Singapore's design and the talents of our designers to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It would increase public understanding and appreciation of the importance of good design.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It would also serve as a hub for experiential learning, academy-industry partnerships and a creative laboratory for design practitioners and overall, boost the growth of Singapore's design sector, which can also be an additional engine in our arts economy.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Gerald Giam can be assured that we have and we will continue to strengthen our quality high-performance sporting ecosystem, for Singapore athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let me elaborate on structures and pathways that we have previously put in place and which we will continue to put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We know that being a full-time athlete in Singapore can sometimes be tough, balancing intense training with competition schedules, often overseas and at the same time, the athlete having to meet other life priorities, often requiring sacrifices to be made.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But it is also rewarding and fulfilling and many of our athletes strive to reach their peak of their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That is why, over the years, we have reshaped and refined our sporting policies and programmes to help mitigate, minimise, if not, remove these trade-offs, enabling our athletes to develop, to train, to compete and to flourish, at the highest levels.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We tap into the sports co-curricular activities in mainstream schools, starting with primary schools, which are often our youths' first exposure to sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We cast the net wide, to identify as much talent as possible at a young age.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And for those who have set their minds on sport from a school age, we have the Singapore Sports School that provides a dedicated specialist environment to support both education and training.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also made this available to high-performance athletes regardless of the school that they are studying in.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, you might be in a different school, but you can come into Sports School for a period or for a season to train for a programme and go back to your original school thereafter.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also put in place a comprehensive sport science and medicine program through the National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) and Singapore Sport Institute (SSI).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ensuring our athletes can manage both the pressures as well as the physicality of high performance sport.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are changes that help to prolong the livelihood and the period of competition at the highest level for our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And they are the latest in our series of efforts that we have made to strengthen high-performance sport in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the years, we have consistently refined this approach, ensuring that athletes have the right infrastructure, adequate resources and multiple opportunities to excel.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And these developments are not just one-off adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They represent a concerted, strategic, long-term commitment to building a sustainable and thriving sports ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I mentioned earlier, we will have the home of Team Singapore as part of the Kallang Alive Masterplan, where all the elements of high-performance sporting development will be integrated in one campus, so athletes can stay, train, study, compete and repeat, until excellence becomes intuition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will also have dedicated access to sport science and nutrition and supported by the relevant NSAs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will significantly strengthen the pillars on which sporting success in Singapore can be advanced.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Members will know, it will take a few years for the home of Team Singapore to materialise under the Kallang Alive Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But we intend to jumpstart the process now.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will enhance our end-to-end service delivery to our athletes across the youth and senior spectrum.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: While the Sports School will remain as a school and retain its brand and identity, this consolidation will more closely integrate Sports School with the rest of the high-performance sporting ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also streamline touchpoints with stakeholders involved through an athlete's life, such as parents and NSAs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will then be able to develop a centrally-coordinated pathway that can provide better visibility and assurance to our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will grow and retain our talents in sport science, sport medicine, administration as well as burgeoning sports technology, which we will harness.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: By having more professional development opportunities to rotate them across sports and profile, and sometimes, it is useful to deploy our sport scientists across different sports, to gain more experience.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These moves will collectively strengthen and deepen the integration between the key aspects of high-performance sport.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will have multiple layers of support converging around the athlete, supporting them through their journey, from youth right through to senior levels and we will, with this programme, be able to hit the ground running once the physical development of the new Kallang Alive Masterplan is completed.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let me conclude my speech with some brief points on the community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In times of crisis, particularly during COVID-19 or the global recession or even in our daily challenges, Singaporeans have shown remarkable generosity, spontaneity, spirit, in both small and big ways, to care for and help each other out.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want to tap on this innate generosity, this strong spirit, as it speaks to the essence of who we are as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As we move forward in SG60 and beyond, it is therefore crucial that we continue to nurture this spirit of contribution and make sure that no one is left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is this sense of empathy and care for fellow citizens that is the hallmark of a progressive and inclusive society, one where we look out for one another as fellow citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To do so and push this along, we are partnering with the National Council of Social Service on the SG SHARE programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This programme multiplies the impact of modest donations over a period of time, to support various social service programmes under the Community Chest.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Beyond monetary donations, we also encourage more Singaporeans to volunteer for causes which are meaningful and which matter to them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With curated volunteering opportunities across a spectrum of different causes, including children, families, seniors, education and sports, we have served more than one million beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also support ground-up initiatives from the community through Our Singapore Fund (OSF).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This fund serves as the seed to kickstart meaningful ideas for Singaporeans, by Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, OSF has helped The New Charis Mission, a non-profit, to expand the reach of "The Unlabelled Run".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The run brings together groups of different backgrounds, with the aim of building an inclusive and compassionate society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Unlabelled Run is just one of the many success stories of OSF.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we look forward to supporting even more of such ground-up projects.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Because of the tenacity of past generations, we are more than just a city.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are a nation, a home, a people who dare to dream, dare to persevere and dare to rise above challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As we honour our past, we must also look ahead to the next bound of our journey.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Singapore of tomorrow will not be built by chance, nor by circumstance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will be built, instead, by all of us – by every artist who expresses our identity, every athlete who pushes the limits of excellence, inspiring us, every young Singaporean who steps forward with a vision and with a voice.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the past five years, I have had the privilege of working alongside my MCCY colleagues in shaping a more inclusive, vibrant and united Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Just as we have done in the past, we have strengthened the ties that bind us, we have championed a Singaporean identity that is confident and outward looking.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through our shared national experiences, we have woven a richer, more interconnected national tapestry, one that tells the story of our people, our passions and our aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is in every Singaporean who comes together – on the field, in the theatre, in our community spaces – to share in something greater than ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is in the stories of our pioneers that we preserve, the dreams of our youth that we nurture and the sense of belonging we create for every Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But this future is not for MCCY alone to build.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, I say this to every Singaporean: your dreams matter, your contributions count and your actions shape our shared destiny.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let us go forward with confidence, with courage and with conviction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Let us embrace the challenges ahead with the same pioneering spirit that has brought us this far.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And together, let us continue weaving our national tapestry – strong, diverse and uniquely Singaporean – into the next great chapter of our story.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We will take clarifications at the end of the speeches.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, you can take your next cut.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Playing and participating in sports is a fun and engaging way to do so.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Granted that as one ages, we may not be able to participate in intense sports activities.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I do not think, for example, I will be diving into any tackles soon on the football pitch.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: However, playing suitable sports and games can promote and enhance our seniors' health.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Popular sports played in the community, include table tennis, badminton or pickleball.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Participating in sports in a safe environment will not only encourage our seniors to have an active and healthier lifestyle but will also aid in mental wellness, continuing to keep our mind active, hone our motor skills and importantly, make more friends in the Community!

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In this context, I invite the Minister to share with us, the Ministry's engagement plans to reach out to more seniors in the community to participate in sports.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Exercise and proper nutrition are essential for not just anyone, but especially seniors in Singapore – for health, independence and quality of life.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Current research shows that regular physical activity strengthens muscles, enhances flexibility and improves balance, reducing the risk of falls and injuries.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Exercise boosts mood lessening anxiety and depression, and improves cognitive function for overall mental health.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: We need to promote health and active participation exercises among seniors, in a safe environment, while catering to their evolving needs.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Developing senior-friendly exercise spaces and providing equipment can also make exercise more accessible.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Providing information on the benefits of exercise and nutrition, along with personalised health plans developed in consultation with healthcare professionals, empowers our seniors to be stewards of their own health.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The Healthier SG initiative offers such support, focusing on physical fitness, nutrition and mental well-being.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: At the same time, encouraging participation in group activities can enhance motivation and provide social support, making exercise and healthy eating more enjoyable and sustainable.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: This is certainly heartening statistics, but I believe we can always do better to help encourage our seniors.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Ministry share an update on the progress of the Disability Sports Master Plan, since it was first introduced in 2016 and its refresh last year, as well as upcoming sporting initiatives to strengthen community integration and foster deeper inclusion?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: The empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) through sports participation represents one of the most meaningful aspects of Singapore's commitment to building an inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Sports has proven to be a powerful vehicle for integration, confidence-building and the breaking down of social barriers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: The benefits of sports programmes that promote inclusivity extend far beyond physical fitness.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: They create platforms for social interaction, foster mutual understanding and demonstrate the remarkable capabilities of PwDs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: These programmes are fundamental to our vision of a Singapore where every individual, regardless of ability, has the opportunity to participate fully in community life.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: While we have made significant strides in developing para-sports and inclusive sporting activities through the Disability Sports Master Plan, we must continue to enhance and expand these opportunities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: This is encouraging but we should do more.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Could the Minister provide an update on current and future efforts to empower people of different abilities through participation in sports together?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Hosting major sporting events like this has great potential to spur Singaporeans to develop a strong interest in sports.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Minister: can MCCY share plans to engage Singaporeans of all ages and encourage them to be interested in sports, to support sports and to take up sports?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: How do we leverage on such world-class events in Singapore to do all these?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: As we look towards this championship and beyond, the preparation of our athletes becomes paramount.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: The journey to sporting excellence is long and demanding, requiring sustained support and strategic planning.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: In this context, I would like to ask the Minister to elaborate on MCCY's plans and strategies to ensure that our Team Singapore athletes are thoroughly prepared for all upcoming major games?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Beyond personal growth, sports provide a platform for social bonding and inclusivity, strengthening relationships among peers and the wider community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: One of the key avenues is to cultivate a positive sports culture where there is a strong emphasis to recognise participation, not just the talent, and at the same time, encouraging and educating parents on the benefits of sports beyond academics.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: This can also include the promotion of traditional sports, such as silat, sepak takraw and even dragon boating, alongside the mainstream sports.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Could MCCY share if there are plans to boost sports participation among school-going children and youths?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Specifically, how can the Ministry encourage greater parental and grassroots engagement and accessibility to sports for young Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is the result of hard work and conscious effort by our founding fathers, who sought to forge unity among disparate communities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Subsequent generations have taken over the mantle, implementing policies that have gradually strengthened our social cohesion and built mutual trust over time.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, as a market-oriented, open economy, there will be, over time, inflows and outflows of foreigners who live and work in our country, alongside fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: These foreigners come from different backgrounds and cultures and take on work in various forms as PMETs, skilled or manual workers.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: It is to be expected that, as foreigners will not intuitively appreciate and understand our Singapore culture and way of life, friction and conflict may result in the community.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In Singapore, we pride ourselves as a diverse and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: It is, therefore, extremely critical that we do our utmost to integrate foreigners into the Singapore society in order to maintain social cohesion and stability.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In this context, I invite the Minister to share the Ministry's plans to strengthen integration of foreigners into our society.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: This is especially relevant as more Singaporeans return to the physical workplace.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, whether we look back 60 years or longer, we will find many threads of generosity and philanthropy in our shared history.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: It was not just among the wealthy and higher income, though many did give generously, but giving was across all income and social levels.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I have often referred to Singapore as a generous society in past speeches.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In the last couple of decades, we have seen philanthropy grow as more and more individuals and families give back to society.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We can and should continue to encourage philanthropy and giving.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore continues to develop as a philanthropic hub for local and international giving.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Could we get an update on existing initiatives and schemes to support the broader charity and non-profit sectors?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In particular, are we seeing an increase in support for arts, heritage, culture and sports?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Are there plans that will build regional giving that will leverage on public and private sector collaboration?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: The enhanced company of good recognition system recognises organisations for demonstrating commitment to corporate purpose and making impact in the areas of people, society, governance, environment and economy.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Could MCCY share whether the recognition system has encouraged more companies to engage in corporate philanthropy and social responsibility?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: How does MCCY plan to encourage more companies to apply to be recognised?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Making monetary giving more convenient and accessible for Singaporeans will help to strengthen financial resilience of charities over the long term.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Can the Ministry share how it plans to make giving monetary donations more convenient and accessible?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: How does the Ministry plan to encourage more residents to make monetary donations?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: SG60 is a significant milestone in our nation's journey.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This anniversary presents a unique opportunity to honour our founding generation while reinvigorating our collective commitment to nation-building.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is a moment to reflect on the values and principles that have guided Singapore's development.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The pioneering spirit, resilience and unity demonstrated by our founding generation have laid the foundation for our success.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As we mark six decades of nationhood, we must ensure that these values continue to inspire and guide future generations.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Our Singapore Fund was launched in 2016 and has been a crucial instrument in empowering citizens to initiate ground-up projects that serve community needs.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As Singapore continues to progress, it is heartening to see individuals, businesses and community groups stepping forward to make a difference.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Our challenge now is to sustain and strengthen this momentum, ensuring that philanthropy and volunteerism remain an integral part of our national identity.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: While we have made good progress, we must continue to do more.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: We should continue to expand our volunteer participation.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How can we encourage more Singaporeans to take part in causes that they care about?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How can we make opportunities more accessible and flexible to suit different lifestyles and interests?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Second, we must continue our efforts of enhancing awareness and the impact of giving.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: By improving transparency and highlighting success stories, we can inspire more people to give with confidence.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Thirdly, we must continue to empower businesses and young changemakers.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Companies and young Singaporeans are stepping up with innovative ways to give back.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How can we strengthen partnerships with the corporate sector and youth-led initiatives to further drive sustainable and impactful contributions towards society?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: What new initiatives are being explored to sustain and enhance philanthropy and volunteerism?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How can we ensure that giving remains inclusive, impactful and meaningful for all?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Together, we can strengthen Singapore's spirit of care and compassion for all.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Mr Chairman, it is important that we continue to nurture our youths and ensure that they remain actively engaged in shaping our collective future.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Singapore's success is built on each generation striving to create a better tomorrow and our young people are the key to drive progress in an ever-changing world.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: It is, therefore, crucial that we continue to empower them, listen to their aspirations and provide platforms for them to contribute meaningfully to society.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: What were some of the key issues that our youths were most passionate about?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As societal needs evolve, how will these panels be enhanced to ensure that they remain relevant and impactful?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: From climate change to mental well-being, from social inclusivity to digital innovation, young Singaporeans have shown great passion in addressing real-world challenges.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Their ideas and enthusiasm must continue to be supported.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How can we further empower them on this journey?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Beyond structured platforms, we must continue to create an environment where young Singaporeans feel that their voices are valued and their actions can make a real difference.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Can MCCY share how it plans to strengthen youth engagement in the years ahead?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How can we ensure that young people from diverse backgrounds, including those who may not typically step forward, are included in these conversations?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How can we deepen partnerships between the Government, community organisations and youth-led initiatives to sustain their momentum?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, Minister Edwin Tong spoke about building a caring, cohesive and confident Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, we have a vibrant arts and heritage scene that Singaporeans can be proud of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I will outline two areas we will focus on to bring Singapore's arts and heritage sector forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, we will expand Singaporeans' access to the arts and encourage all, from the young to the old, to participate in and appreciate our vibrant local arts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second, we will strengthen support for our arts and heritage workers and businesses and empower them to shape an enduring future for our arts and heritage ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Under the Arts Plan 2.0, we aim to build a Connected Society and a Distinctive City through the arts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: A key part of this is bringing the arts to every part of our city.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We launched the ArtsEverywhere@CDC initiative last year and brought high-quality performances into places where Singaporeans live, work and play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through ArtsEverywhere@CDC, Singaporeans with little or no exposure to the arts have gained a newfound appreciation for both the arts and the Singapore culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Mdm Yang Siew Shan, an engineer who lives in Woodlands, discovered a new interest in the arts after attending an ArtsEverywhere performance in her neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For 67-year-old Mdm Jamaliah, she felt a sense of pride in her culture when she watched NADI Singapura's traditional Malay drumming performance in Brickland Estate with her friends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas asked about encouraging cross-cultural appreciation and engagement through the arts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure her ArtsEverywhere@CDC is a key platform for this purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: ArtsEverywhere@CDC performances have featured arts groups from different cultures, such as Indian ensemble Brahmastra; Chinese traditional ensemble Ding Yi; and the Philharmonic Winds Orchestra.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: ArtsEverywhere@CDC also includes fringe activities, where arts groups provide audiences, participants with more immersive cultural experiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Brahmastra’s performances were accompanied by a Parai and Karagam Workshop, where participants learned to play the parai, a traditional Indian percussion instrument; and perform the karakattam, an ancient Indian folk dance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NADI Singapura also ran a Paper Tanjak Workshop, where participants of all background or races could create their very own traditional Malay headgear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Beyond physical spaces, we will also bring the arts into the virtual world.
