speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas asked about the plans to enable our arts practitioners to use technology to reach younger audiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As part of Arts Plan 2.0, NAC launched Project Arts Metaverse, an Alliance-for-Action to co-create arts experiences in virtual spaces with the arts and tech community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, NAC will support and develop three pilot projects that allow our artists to experiment with new ways of making art and nurturing new audiences, especially among young people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While we invest in bringing the arts and culture to all Singaporeans, we also want to encourage them to attend local arts and cultural events and activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is why Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister Edwin Tong shared more about the introduction of the SG Culture Pass.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are proud of our unique Singapore arts and culture, and we call on all Singaporeans to "support local".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Beyond this, we also hope to continue fostering cultural philanthropy through the Cultural Matching Fund (CMF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To date, we have disbursed more than $400 million in dollar-for-dollar matching grants to 127 unique charities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This means, almost eight in 10 arts and heritage charities have received such grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The number of donations matched by CMF has multiplied from 2,000 in Year 2014 to more than 16,000 in 2024.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas asked if CMF could be expanded to match earned income and if matching grants can be broadened.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The CMF encourages philanthropic giving to Singapore's arts and heritage sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: CMF grants fund expenses which are directly related to the delivery of programmes by arts and heritage groups because we want to ensure that public monies deliver impact for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Expenses, like legal fees, staff bonuses and welfare benefits, are not covered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This applies only to the matching grants, not to the donations raised by the charities and IPCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The CMF is just one of many schemes administered by MCCY and NAC, that our arts and heritage groups can use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Minister Edwin Tong talked about the new SG Culture Pass, for example, focuses on helping our arts and culture groups increase their earned income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, we will continue to foster and encourage arts participation among our children and students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, NAC and Ministry of Education (MOE) introduced the Artist-in-School Scheme and the Arts Education Programme (AEP) in MOE schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC also worked with MOE to introduce Museum-Based Learning in primary schools and Performing Arts-Based Learning for lower secondary students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our cultural institutions offer many programmes for children, such as the National Gallery of Singapore's Children's Biennale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2022, you will remember that we opened the Children's Museum, the first local museum dedicated to children aged 12 and younger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To help parents promote and participate in the arts with their children, NAC provides recommendation on family-friendly arts events and experiences on Catch.sg.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As suggested by Ms Hany Soh, we will bring these benefits further upstream to include preschoolers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will scale up the AEP in Government-supported preschools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Currently, more than 500 Government-supported preschools are on the board AEP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, the arts is a powerful force to help elderly people and residents live well and age well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government has been investing in this area as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, NAC's WeCare Arts Fund supports Social Service Agencies providing arts programmes that strengthen the physical and the mental well-being of elderly people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Fund has supported more than 80 programmes, including batik painting, dance, ukulele sessions for more than 1,500 beneficiaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC is currently collaborating with SingHealth Community Hospitals and the AIC to develop a framework and resources to guide the design of arts programmes that promote well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, MCCY is dedicated and committed to supporting our arts and heritage practitioners and helping them realise their full potential as Mr Fahmi Aliman and Mr Darryl David have suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In fact, this is what Creative Economy pillar of the Arts Plan 2.0 is all about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will: one, expand our support for the next generation of Singaporean artists; two, ensure that our arts and culture workers have the right skillsets and capabilities; and three, support our arts and culture companies in growing their businesses to bring the sector to new heights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government has consistently supported the development of artistic talent in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the past three years, NAC has invested over $5 million in talent development programmes, including scholarships, international residencies and the Young Artist Award (YAA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These initiatives have supported more than 400 local artists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These investments have added more talents to our pool of arts and culture practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, Mr Adib Kosnan received the NAC scholarship in Year 2023 to pursue a Master of Arts in Arts Pedagogy and Practice at LASALLE College of the Arts (LASALLE).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I met him in 2023 when he received his scholarship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Adib is an Associate Artist at a local theatre company, Checkpoint Theatre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Taken together, this will support around 40 more students to pursue higher arts education each year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will help them upskill and stay ahead in today's fast-evolving landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, the arts sector is about 19,000 strong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They have diverse backgrounds, talents, capabilities and skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Around the world, the creative sector has always led the wider economy in terms of project-based and freelance work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many arts practitioners, including some of our most talented, are Self-Employed Persons (SEPs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They comprise about a third of the arts sector workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will ensure that our arts workforce has the right capabilities to bring the sector forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will: number one, expand the resources available to our arts SEPs; number two, develop a robust leadership pipeline in the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will expand its offerings through the Arts Resource Hub (ARH), which was set up in 2019 to help arts SEPs establish their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Currently, more than 3,400 arts SEPs subscribe to ARH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Subscribers enjoy free access to co-working spaces, preferential rental rates on performances and rehearsal spaces, as well as updates on ARH programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They also receive career and professional development support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the next phase of ARH, NAC will work with our arts community to shape ARH offerings across artforms and career stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Jean See asked about how MCCY will work with stakeholders to improve freelancers' mental health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure her that we are doing more in this area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In 2024, ARH conducted a series of peer-sharing sessions with arts collective CITRUS Practices, focusing on self-care tools as well as practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Going forward, we will expand ARH initiatives to cover issues, such as improving working conditions for arts practitioners, legal issues including protecting intellectual property (IP), IP rights and developing well-being resources for mental resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition to developing individual talents, we also want to build up our arts companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Like corporates in any sector, arts companies need business and management capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This may be even more crucial in the arts sector, where economics are challenging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will introduce targeted support to develop a robust leadership pipeline in the arts sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is critical as most arts companies are micro-enterprises without dedicated human resource capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the next three years, we aim to equip a core of arts managers for leadership roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over time, we want to cultivate stronger leadership bench to catalyse further growth in the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Elevating our arts and heritage sector requires more than developing individual talents and supporting organisational capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In particular, the Government can play a role to stimulate demand for heritage goods and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked how the Government will support our heritage businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They will receive brand campaign support, as well as access to business support, such as consultancy services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, I want to invite heritage business owners and members of the public to submit nominations for SG Heritage Businesses so that we can recognise, celebrate and support these businesses in our communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, please allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Singapore's arts and heritage are pillars of our social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They bring us together, help us understand each other and give us a shared sense of belonging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Singapore celebrates its 60th year of Independence this year, let us look forward to the next phase of nation and community building through arts and heritage, ensuring all citizens have access to arts while strengthening support for arts and heritage workers and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The ArtsEverywhere@CDC programme, jointly launched by the National Arts Council (NAC), Community Development Councils (CDCs) and People's Association (PA), is a platform that provides Singaporeans with opportunities to experience arts and culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government will continue to fund this programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, ArtsEverywhere@CDC will present over 200 performances across various community neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Beyond increasing access to the arts, we will also promote the well-being of seniors through arts programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC is working with SingHealth Community Hospitals (SCH) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) to develop frameworks and provide resources to guide the design of arts programmes that promote well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are piloting arts programmes in four Active Ageing Centres (AACs) and the Outram Community Hospital, which use different arts forms such as visual arts, storytelling, music, and dance to engage seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the coming year, we will expand the pilots to more AACs, integrating arts into community activities to promote citizens' well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, MCCY will also pilot the SG Heritage Business Scheme to recognise exemplary heritage businesses, help citizens better appreciate long established local heritage businesses, products and services, take pride in their achievements and support the development of local heritage businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Businesses that have been in operation for at least 30 years, provide locally rooted trades, goods or services, and contribute significantly to the identity of a community or place can be designated as SG Heritage Businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These recognised businesses will receive brand campaign support and access to business support, such as consultancy service subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We welcome community organisations and the public to actively submit nominations for SG Heritage Businesses, so that we can continue to support these businesses and acknowledge their contributions to our cultural heritage with our actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The measures I have announced today aim to bring arts and heritage to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Through these activities and programmes, we hope to unite our people, encourage more people to join in our local arts and heritage, and contribute to the richness of our unique culture. : Chairman, our arts and heritage scene has come a long way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, on any given day, Singaporeans can watch a performance in the heartlands, attend an arts exhibition, or walk into any one of our excellent museums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We aim to bring the arts and heritage to all Singaporeans and enable more Singaporeans to appreciate and contribute to the richness of our unique culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Chairman, Mr Edwin Tong spoke of how our shared experiences weave a rich tapestry capturing the stories and dreams of our people and our nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I experienced this recently at ART SG when weaving a small part of a 60-metre-long tapestry on display.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This tapestry was made from upcycled fabrics by UBS employees, community partners and children from Care Corner in a bid to commemorate SG60.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is a great example of how arts and heritage and culture, in fact, bring Singapore and Singaporeans together to contribute to our rich culture, as Senior Minister of State Low has just described in her speech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It represents how we weave together diverse races, religions, generations and perspectives into a rich tapestry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And today, we benefit from the strong social fabric that they have woven.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Like the generations before us, we must weave a stronger and tighter social fabric, pulling different threads together to contribute to this tapestry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we have a long tradition of communities coming together to do well and to do good, a tradition that is older than our nation, of collective responsibility and mutual support which is a key thread in our social fabric.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since 1925, our co-ops have played a critical role in building our nation and our social compact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, our first co-ops were formed to help junior civil servants meet unexpected expenses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, we have a much wider and a much richer landscape of co-ops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And they cover a diversity of needs, from daily necessities to seniors' recreation and to help individuals with special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Co-ops like the Runninghour Co-operative, which is an inclusive sports co-op that promotes the integration of persons with special needs through sports.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Runninghour was founded in 2009 as a running club with just 10 members with special needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Today, Runninghour has grown and has over 780 registered members, including persons with special needs, volunteers and more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: A good friend I have known since we were teenagers who lost his sight in his 20s is an active member.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, we celebrate the centenary year of our co-op movement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And over the past 100 years, many of our social needs have been better addressed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But others are emerging, including our demographic challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our co-ops, too, now face a myriad of challenges; new, different challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They face greater competition, rapid digitalisation and changing consumer needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Therefore, our co-ops must transform to attract and retain talent and to extend their reach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To do good, our co-ops must continue to do well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I meet with them regularly to chat with them and to learn and to engage with them and to see how we can better support them as they continue to do good and continue to do well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, over the last Saturday, I met with the Amalgamated Union of Public Employees Credit Cooperative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This roadmap will help to extend our co-ops' social mission and impact, help them to develop talent and strengthen governance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, just as we are tightening our weave through our co-op sector, we will also encourage this spirit of mutual care through philanthropy – questions that Mr Keith Chua and Ms Jean See had raised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will continue growing philanthropy through tax deductions and dollar-for-dollar matching grants like our Cultural Matching Fund and our One Team Singapore Fund.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Tote Board's Enhanced Fund-Raising Programme likewise supports fundraising efforts of all eligible Singapore-registered charities, while our SG Gives' matching grant encourages donations to support social and community programmes serving communities in need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These will all galvanise more donations and amplify the impact of giving on our charities and communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And through National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre's (NVPC's) Company of Good recognition system, we recognised 290 companies last year, in 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is double the number in 2022, and it includes four times the number of SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, it is not just the multinational companies (MNCs) and the large companies but also SMEs, and we have been encouraging that.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: All of these companies, regardless of their size, actively integrate social impact into their operations, and they give their time, talents, treasures – and it amounts to a combined total donation of around $323 million, and over 800,000 volunteer hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will encourage more companies to make doing good a core part of their business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And one way we are expanding our tapestry is by connecting communities in an increasingly fractured world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: That is why we are hosting the third edition of the International Conference on Cohesive Societies (ICCS) in June.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked how ICCS 2025 can facilitate deeper understandings of multiculturalism and interfaith harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In fact, our youth leaders will join the working committee of the Young Leaders Programme at ICCS to facilitate breakout sessions and hold cultural sharings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I recently spoke to a group of youths about the importance of our precious, hard-won racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our community leaders will also share their lived experiences of harmony in diversity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: At 60 years, we are still a young nation and have much to learn from others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I have been involved with earlier ICCS editions and have witnessed the impact that it has made in Singapore and beyond our shores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through ICCS 2025, we get to share our challenges, learnings and brainstorm solutions and areas for improvement in a never-ending effort to remain open and connected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Like Conal McMahon, PwC's Head of Market Insights.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He told me he moved to Singapore about seven years ago after living in Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong and Shanghai.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He and his wife were attracted by Singapore's lifestyle and personal growth opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In his free time, Conal teaches professional skills at Aidha, a charity looking after migrant domestic workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Conal also serves on the board of the Jane Goodall Institute, which empowers youth to take action for the environment, for the animals and community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is wonderful to have people like Conal call Singapore home and contribute to our nation and our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we too, must welcome our overseas friends with open arms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I understand, having lived overseas for over nine years across my career.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While overseas, the community surrounding me and my young family helped us to settle down and find home in that particular city, for that particular season.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Newcomers to Singapore alike also navigate unfamiliarity every day.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we can all play our part to make them feel at home in that particular season of their lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked how we are fostering greater understanding and integration of foreigners in our society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I co-chair this with PwC Singapore's Chairman, Mr Marcus Lam, who serves in the Singapore National Employers Federation and Singapore Business Federation; alongside 15 other industry representatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We began engagements last year – we have met quite a few times now, including in focus group discussions and we have so far gleaned some learnings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, local employers are committed to fair, equal-opportunity hiring; they want to better integrate employees and foster positive interactions in workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Foreign professionals also want to adapt to Singapore's cultural norms and build relationships with their local colleagues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And efforts have already begun, so we have a running start.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I recently spoke with Diallo Ramatoulaye, a Canadian lady originally from Mali.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through SIP, Rama deepened her understanding of our culture and our work ethic, and built meaningful relationships with her local colleagues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: She is giving back to Singapore through teaching financial management to children with special needs and also befriending underprivileged families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our AfA will rally and equip more employers to nurture inclusive workplace communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we will share more about what we have learned and what we plan to do in the second half of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also plan to refresh our Integration and Naturalisation Committees and Champions (INC) programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since 2006, INC volunteers have helped newcomers settle into their communities and adapt to our Singaporean way of life, including Ms Jessica Tjung from my constituency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Jessica is a Singaporean Citizen originally from Indonesia and has lived here for over 26 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Her first-hand experiences navigating integration's challenges led her to volunteer as an Integration and Naturalisation Champion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Jessica has spearheaded initiatives, like an Old School Games Carnival in 2023, for residents of all ages and backgrounds to learn about our heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Like Conal, Rama and Jessica, every thread contributes unique colour and texture to our Singapore tapestry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths bring fresh colour and perspective and are our future leaders, who will take on the work of tightening our weave and expanding our tapestry into the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Shawn Huang asked about our Youth Panels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our inaugural Youth Panels gave our youths a platform to be involved in policy-making.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And our youths have responded with great interest – 120 youths stepped forward to work with the Government to deliberate on policy issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We put together four panels, together with our youths, we called them #LifeHacks, #JobHacks, #TechHacks and #GreenHacks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: At one of my many engagements with these energetic Youth Panels, I spoke with Kimberly Quek, who is a final year Life Science student at the National University of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Despite her hearing loss, Kimberly has excelled in her pursuits in bowling and passions in the sustainability space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To Mr Shawn Huang's question, we are also reviewing the Panels to better involve our youths in shaping Singapore's future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Youth Panels have concluded and I recently hosted them here, in Parliament, to deep dive into their recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We had a really lively dialogue, and they gave excellent solutions and also recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And, in fact, it does not end here, because many of the Youth Panel leaders have gone on to thread new pathways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: One of them, Josh Lee, was a contributor to our #TechHacks Panel, and now serves as a youth representative to the Media Literacy Council.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, there is a channel for them to contribute even more to national initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Just as we have empowered youths, like Josh, through the Youth Panels, we are doing the same for other youths through Mentoring SG, our national mentoring movement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we are doing more, there is good momentum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are doing more to guide our youths through life's key transition stages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are now partnering with Institutes of Higher Learning to match more youths with mentors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We launched the first Youth Mentoring Hub at Singapore Polytechnic in November that will connect 10,000 students to mentors over the next three years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Companies or corporates, like Jobstreet by SEEK and Prudential, offer flash mentoring at career roadshows, and they provide valuable insights as our youths prepare for work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also partnered trade associations and chambers, like the Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association, to promote mentoring to the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) students and to attract future semi-conductor leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I have attended these sessions over the years at ITE College Central many times and saw firsthand how interested our youths are in exposing themselves to new opportunities in the semi-conductor space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We invite everyone to join us as mentors – we will not leave you hanging, because we will train you.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: You can pick up mentoring skills through our Mentoring 101 programme and Workforce Skills Qualification-accredited Mentoring for Youth course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This SG60 year, we are embarking on a year-long series on engagements with our youths, for them to step forward to share their views and realise their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These are platforms for our youths to connect on what Singapore can be for them and how they want to contribute in areas, such as volunteerism and mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Every youth is invited to participate and be a change maker in an area that interest them and is close to their hearts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are committed to enable more to "Live Better Through Sport", by making sports programmes and facilities accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I will cover initiatives to boost sports participation among three groups: children and youth, persons with disabilities and seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Mohd Fahmi will be glad to know that we have been and will continue to expand the opportunities for our children and youth to play sports, both in and outside of schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We partner MOE to promote sports in schools through programmes, such as the Strategic Partnership Co-Curricular Activity (SP-CCA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This enables students to pursue CCAs beyond what their school offers and, at the same time, encourages inter-school mixing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As mentioned at MOE's COS, we have expanded SP-CCA to include canoeing and we plan to add hockey by 2026.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Outside schools, children can engage in sports through the ActiveSG Academies and Clubs (A&Cs) and lower income families may tap on the SportCares Bursary to fully cover programme fees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Children and youths can take part in sports activities and interest groups organised by the People's Association's Community Sports Networks, such as the PAssion Community Football Programme for children aged five to 16 years old or the PA Community Championship and Pesta Sukan for youths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also work with National Sports Associations (NSAs), private academies and sport clubs to broaden the sports programmes available to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chairman, let me next move on to sports for PwDs, a topic Mr Baey Yam Keng and Mr Ong Hua Han spoke about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Sports enhances quality of life for PwDs and can help transform societal attitudes toward disability, by spotlighting strengths, instead of disability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We first launched the Disability Sports Master Plan in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This plan focuses on three "A"s: first, to increase accessibility; second, to raise awareness; and last but not least, to fulfil aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, we will continue to increase accessibility by further increasing the capacity of our disability sport programmes and make ActiveSG sports facilities more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Take Ms Diana Yap and her son, Aaron, whom I recently met, for example.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Diana shared that Aaron did not like playing sports initially but fell in love with badminton since joining SportSG's Play-Ability and now looks forward to every single badminton session!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With better outreach, we hope that more PwDs can enjoy sports like Aaron!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Third, we want to support the aspirations of PwDs who desire and have the potential to pursue sports at the high-performance level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to build the capabilities of disability sport coaches and support personnel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also establish a para-sport National Training Centre within the home of TeamSG at Kallang Alive and set up Para Sports Community Hubs across the island so that PwDs can access sports closer to home. \We have set up five such community hubs to date and plan to add more.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These hubs are intentionally set up at ActiveSG centres, so that both PwDs and members of the public can enjoy sports together in the same space.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I was told that this has actually allowed for PwDs to make friends with members of the public and this integration is exactly what we hope to see.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We target to have at least $10 million in the fund by 2030, where $5 million will be raised through donations and the other $5 million matched dollar-for-dollar by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We encourage everyone to contribute actively to this Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With this comes a growing concern – frailty, a condition which reduces the function and health of older individuals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aside from inactivity, poor nutrition and social isolation, frailty is related to muscle loss, also known as sarcopenia, which begins as early as when we are in our 30s or 40s.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And by the age of 70, we may lose up to about 25% of our muscle mass!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In response to Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Darryl David and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, I would like to share about the Active Health initiative and its Frailty Prevention Programme (FPP), which was introduced by SportSG in collaboration with AIC and features an eight-week Combat Age Related Loss of Muscle (CALM) programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Seniors in the programme participate in exercises involving resistance bands and dumb bells, along with guidance on nutrition and sleep.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The FPP also offers adaptive sports such as sport stacking, ladder toss, boccia, disc golf and seated floorball – activities which are modified to enable players of differing abilities to participate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aside from providing a good workout, these sports promote teamwork and interaction amongst seniors, reducing the risks of isolation and loneliness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To bring sports to seniors where they are, FPP is being conducted at Active Ageing Centres in our communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To ensure successful roll out, we aim to train staff and volunteers from all Active Ageing Centres who come onboard the FPP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From my chats with seniors, I have heard directly from them about how the FPP has improved their lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Recently, I met Mdm Tham Yoke Cheng, Mdm May Mak and Mdm Lam Ngiat Yin who were participating in the CALM programme at Chong Hua Tong Active Ageing Centres in Moulmein Cairnhill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I was glad to hear that CALM has helped them to strengthen their muscles and improve their walking gait, especially for Mdm Lam who has issues with her knees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For Mdm Mak, she even shared that she had mostly stayed at home for the past three years before joining the programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Now, thanks to CALM, Mdm Mak likes to bake treats to share with her fellow seniors at Active Ageing Centres!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through my visits, I have also seen the enthusiasm that seniors have for adaptive sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I have played many of these games and lost many games with them!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, for seniors who have joined CALM or adaptive sports and enjoyed it, I encourage all of you to invite your friends to join in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I also look forward to more Active Ageing Centres offering both the CALM and adaptive sports programmes at your centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Exercise not only keeps us physically healthy, but also help maintains our mental acuity and agility, making our lives more fulfilling.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To help seniors actively participate in sports, SportSG and AIC have specially launched the Frailty Prevention Programme, which includes the eight-week CALM programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These courses are conducted at Active Ageing Centres located in our neighbourhoods, where professional coaches provide careful guidance through exercise, nutrition and good lifestyle habits to help our seniors maintain a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Seniors who have participated in the programme have reported significant benefits, noting improvements in both their physical strength and quality of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I hope they share the benefits of this programme with their friends and family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We welcome seniors who have not yet participated in this programme to sign up at their nearest Active Ageing Centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Let us enjoy our golden years together through staying active, interacting with those around us and exercising actively! : Sir, through the Sports Facilities Master Plan, we aim to provide most Singaporeans with affordable sport facilities no more than a 10-minute walk from their homes by around 2030.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked for an update on this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This includes two sheltered basketball courts and four open surface courts at the new ActiveSG Sport Park @ Bedok North, which will open later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In addition, this year, residents in Ang Mo Kio and Queenstown can also soon enjoy renovated facilities in their neighbourhood at the Queenstown Sport Centre and ActiveSG Sport Park @ Ang Mo Kio.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Sport-In-Precinct (SIP) initiative is yet another key strategy by SportSG to bring facilities closer to Singaporeans and their families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Out of these, six SIPs are already under construction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Residents in Keat Hong, Tampines North, Pasir Ris East, Whampoa, Ulu Pandan and Choa Chu Kang can look forward to their completion over the next few years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To keep pace with demographic shifts, we will also build sport facilities that cater better to the needs of seniors and working adults.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: An example is the upcoming "Active Health Fitness Trail" at Mei Ling, which has specially designed equipment and architecture to create a safe and effective exercise environment for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is an important feature of the broader Health District @ Queenstown.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To ensure fair access, SportSG introduced the MyActiveSG+ booking platform in June last year, as pointed out by Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Faisal Manap.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The new platform addresses concerns that some users were abusing scripts to monopolise bookings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Now, everyone can only have one account tagged to their Singpass and peak hour slots are allocated by ballot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This ensures that everyone has an equal chance of booking their preferred slot and facilities, which has also increased the number of individuals with successful bookings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also enhanced the platform, based on feedback, adding features like high-demand indicators and improved search filters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We continue to welcome feedback as we continue to work to improve the platform.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To conclude, Sir, I have spoken several times in the past in this Chamber about how through sport, one can defy the odds and redefine the deck of cards that life deals each of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In past COS, I have shared about the story of boccia para-athlete, Aloysius Gan who despite being quadriplegic and non-verbal, shows us clearly that the human spirit triumphs disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We need to start from young and we can start with each of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Let us make inclusion not just a goal, but a living and breathing part of who we are.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I think four concerts in May this year.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I like to ask the Minister if he can provide more information on this and in particular, whether the Government is giving any grants for these concerts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They negotiated directly with the artist and her team, including Live Nation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just have two clarifications for Minister Edwin.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I spent six years as an educator at Temasek Polytechnic's School of Design and during that time I developed not just a deep understanding of the significance of design, but also an understanding of the role that design played in the history of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, when I heard about the Minister's speech that we are going to have a dedicated design museum in Singapore, it was certainly heartening news.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My clarifications are, Sir: are there any particular designers or design disciplines that this design museum will focus on, for example, interior architecture, interior design, product design, fashion design, for example?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And also the second clarification is, how will the curation of the material in this design museum differ from other design-related exhibitions that are currently on display in other museums, for example, I believe that the Asian Civilisation Museum has a fashion display.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That would include also the concept, the curatorial element and direction, as well as the kinds of exhibits, both permanent as well as temporary, that we will have.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But in my speech earlier, I gave an idea of the kinds of designs that we are thinking about – fashion, jewellery, architecture, industrial, furniture – all of which have Singaporeans' involvement in one form or another.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would say, last year, as a side trip to the Venice Biennale, I visited the Milan Design Week as well and saw one dedicated booth for Singaporean designers to showcase their exhibits.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I saw quite well-designed and well-functioning furniture designs by Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is one area that we can think about because we do have very well-regarded and well-known designers in that space.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Likewise, in jewellery, as I mentioned, and also in fashion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, overall, we will think about this as a combination of both permanent designs that will resonate with the Singaporean audience, but also temporary ones that allow regional and international designers to anchor their exhibitions in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said, to create a hub and a centre of gravity for the design space in Singapore and, through Singapore, for the region as well.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: My first clarification is for Minister Edwin Tong and it is on the use of the Culture Pass for the purchase of books.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: I understand Minister Tong's explanation that the Culture Pass is primarily for participatory experiences.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: And if I understand him correctly, the reading of books is a primary way in which someone participates in literary arts and this is why book purchases will be covered by the Culture Pass.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: But I would just like to take the opportunity to make the point that the purchase and consumption of visual art can also be a participatory experience that is very similar in the way that one might consume a book.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: So, when you buy a local painting or an artwork, you typically try to interpret, analyse and connect with it.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: In fact, art historians refer to this process as "reading the artwork".

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: So, the terminology that you use is actually identical to what you would use when you are talking about consuming a book.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: The physical experience is also very similar if you are buying an artwork from a gallery.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: Many small local galleries do not charge an admission fee for you to enter.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: So, just like you would enter a bookshop, find a book that connects with you, buy it, take it home, appreciate it and consume it, I think the same can be said for purchases of visual art as well.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: So, with all of these taken into account, would the Minister be open to reconsidering the exclusion that is presently in place for the purchases of visual art using the Culture Pass credit?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: My second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: So, I would be grateful if she could please address that and reply to my cut.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: She has been pushing several points and I appreciate that very much because she comes from the perspective of someone who is engaged with the arts industry, understanding the needs and oftentimes, coming to Parliament to portray those needs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On her specific point, I understand the point she made about appreciating artworks, visual artworks and one way of doing that, of course, is to buy those artworks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We made a distinction for books because it is quite different.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You can still take part in exhibitions, galleries, there can be events that centre around visual arts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we decided to not include the Culture Pass for the financial purchase of visual artworks for the reasons I have outlined.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank Ms Usha Chandradas for the opportunity for me to respond to her question on the salary guidelines.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Please allow me to explain that the nature of employment, as well as the wage structure in the arts versus the social service sector, are really quite different.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But I also want to use this opportunity to assure the Member that MCCY publishes the Singapore Cultural Statistics annually.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And there is a section on creative economy data which includes figures for the number of arts and culture companies and societies, employment numbers, and also wage numbers, value-added and operating receipts.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We do not just work within the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We work very closely with the sector as well as the Department of Statistics and also the Ministry of Manpower.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These studies are important to MCCY and NAC because they inform our understanding of the complex factors and issues that influence the salaries and employment in the arts sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, we have used these data and insights to develop programmes, including a programmes that has been announced during this COS.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to reassure Ms Usha Chandradas that we will certainly continue to monitor jobs and skills data for the arts sector and share this with the stakeholders in the arts and culture ecosystem and work together to design our policies and programme accordingly.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Chairman, this is pertaining to my earlier cuts to the Minister in relation to the progress of the NHB's Heritage Trails project and whether it has plans to expand to feature stories of how local community clubs have evolved and touched our lives over the years and more specifically, whether a heritage trail marker can be placed at Woodgrove's Fuchun Community Club to mark its history of being Singapore's first rural community centre since 1963.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I look forward to the Minister's favourable reply.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Minister Edwin Tong has asked me to help to relay this.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Ms Hany Soh has talked about this last year as well and she will probably remember that during last year's COS, we said that more than 24 heritage trails have been launched.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And in fact, during last year's COS, I also talked about the Heritage Activation Nodes (HAN).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MCCY and NHB want to thank her for her interest.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And I want to assure her that NHB will continue to work with the communities, including her team, and potentially explore ways to commemorate community spaces, including Fuchun Community Club.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: First is, even with top coaching and facilities, our athletes may still lack a strong local training and competitive environment.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: This is because Singapore's small population and even smaller pool of young athletes aiming for world-class success limits their chances to train with equally driven peers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But this is not feasible for most families, especially those from lower- and middle-income groups.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: So, how is SportSG tackling this challenge beyond just financial support by building a stronger local training and competition environment across all sports?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Second, there are currently only 10 academy programme sports at the Singapore Sports School.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: With the school's move to the Kallang campus, are there plans to increase the number of academy programme sports?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We do want to push our athletes beyond the local sphere, and those who surpass the standards that are being offered locally, we want to push them overseas, because the more you push them into difficult environments where they have to level up, meet better opponents, stronger opponents, the better prepared they will be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, our principle has always been to drive our athletes to train and if necessary, compete overseas as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Earlier on in his speech, Mr Giam mentioned two of our badminton players.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, they are still on the road after the German Open.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the middle tier, what we do is to organise training trips overseas where possible.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We group them together, whether as an NSA-initiated exercise or in some cases where ActiveSG has academies, we group them together as academy-initiated exercise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we try and take the initiative to take them overseas for greater exposure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other cases, on occasion, we bring in foreign coaches to lend their expertise on local soil.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That allows us to have more outreach, and we touch more trainees and more athletes can benefit from the presence of foreign coaches.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Again, from time to time, NSAs, when they identify a good foreign coach to come in, either at the developmental level or at the high-performance level, we also support the NSAs to hire these coaches to bring even bigger impact to the pipeline.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these are among some of the measures that we take to expose our athletes, the junior ones as well as the senior ones, to a greater variety of different training environments, as well as to foreign input and foreign thinking on the sport.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of these would help to level up the playing field and expose our athletes to greater competition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That leads me to the Member's second question.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Chairman, I have two clarifications for the Minister of State and one clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: To Minister of State, I would like to ask: how does MCCY plan to encourage more companies to come on board the company of Good Recognition System, and also whether MCCY has plans to actually work with the MyCareersFuture Singapore, and also other jobseeker portals, such that these companies that are recognised as company of good are actually elevated as choice employers?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: To the Senior Minister of State, I would like to ask because many of our freelance coaches and instructors are actually directly engaged by Government procuring entities, such as schools, and we know that there is actually a Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health and Well-being.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: So, my question is whether there can be more efforts taken such that these Government procuring entities, such as schools, can work very closely with our freelancers by taking reference to this Tripartite Advisory?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That is a good trend and we will continue to spur them on.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: One initial challenge in the early days was to get more SMEs involved, and we now have SME representation within that Company of Good Roundtable, which I sit in.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And through that, we are also getting more SMEs to be involved.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will discuss with both the MNCs and LLEs as well as the SMEs to see whether we can do more on that front.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank Ms Jean See for her clarification.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure her that there is ongoing collaboration and discussion between MCCY as well as MOE.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I recall that when I came back to MCCY for my second stint from July 2020, if you remember, it was during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with my NAC and NHB colleagues, we strengthened our collaboration and also synergised, and really strengthened the nexus between the Ministry and MOE.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MOE, as we know, especially at the primary and secondary schools, have arts and culture instructors, music instructors, sports instructors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We were very happy to also rope in the National Instructors and Coaches Association.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Even post COVID-19 pandemic, we have leveraged on that strong infrastructure between MCCY, NAC, NHB, as well as SportsSG and also MOE.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Under the AEP, we have many arts and culture, and music instructors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And indeed, we do want to continue to leverage on this partnership to persuade the schools to also ensure that there is buy-in and they hoist on board the Tripartite Guidance and Advisory.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: On behalf of the heartland merchants, since I am the advisor for the Federation of Merchants’ Associations, I would like to ask MCCY how many businesses are expected to benefit from this scheme?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And what is the budget for this scheme?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: And are there plans to expand it beyond Chinatown, Kampong Glam and Little India, to include other areas like Joo Chiat and Katong?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank the Member, Mr Henry Quek, for this clarification.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Most of them are concentrated in the central area that will benefit from these concerted efforts to support and grow our heritage businesses, especially the heritage business in Singapore's historic precinct.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, you raised your hand earlier?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: First, do we expect the merger of NYSI, SSI and ultimately, the Singapore Sports School to impact existing staff in any of the current organisations, and more specifically, do we expect any retrenchment of staff?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Second, what are MCCY plans for the Singapore Sports School post-merger?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Specifically, will the merger impact the support that will be received by our student athletes?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: I also have a question for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua on the CALM and adaptive sports programmes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You heard me also say just now that we intend and have gone upstream in terms of our spexPotential to open up the pool of athletes that will qualify for spexPotential and support them earlier on their journey.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, if anything is to come out of this, it is in fact serving more athletes than less and to also grow the expertise in areas such as sports administration, sports management and also sports science.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have an intention to grow the number of sports scientists per capita number of athletes that we have in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, really the move is one in the mode of expanding rather than contracting.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On Mr Xie's point about the impact of sports school and the merger, the intention is for sports school to provide the educational arm of an athlete's journey.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, if you think about it in terms of where it is today: today's Sports School sits in Woodlands; SSI sits in Kallang; we have the NSA spread across Singapore with some training facilities in Kallang, and others outside.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The idea is to consolidate all into one campus so that end-to-end the support for junior as well as senior athlete, from the time you start education until you graduate from school, but remain in the sport, all of that can be centred into one venue, one campus, for a holistic and specialised training regime for all our athletes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: While the seniors are at the Centres, they can make use of all the other programmes as well as facilities like swimming pools, gyms, that are also made available free of charge for our seniors who are 65 and above.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In addition, there are other programmes, for instance, SportCare conducts adaptive morning exercises.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: These are conducted on a weekly basis at the locations that are near where seniors live.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, this is just another example of how we are engaging seniors at locations and with programmes which are convenient for them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I have two clarifications for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The first: I am very happy to hear about ICCS and the involvement of our youth.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: How is MCCY working with more youth to be more involved in local interfaith activities?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Second clarification: you mentioned the AfA for integration of foreign professionals and also refreshing of our INCs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: What would this refresh entail, and when can we get more details of this?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: He is part of our IRO youth team, and they have just refreshed it and are doing a lot more.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It gives them this platform for them to share with an international audience and international peers what interfaith and multiculturalism is like in Singapore, and also gives them opportunity to take the lead in some of these discussions, showcase what Singapore is doing, but also learn and pick up lessons from others.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The second question is with regard to the INC.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We think that it is time for us to also refresh it.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have refreshed our initiatives over the years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we are going to do a pilot.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is going to be in my constituency in Moulmein-Cairnhill.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will learn from the learnings from this pilot, and hopefully, share it across the island.

speaker: The Chairman
text: As there are no more clarifications, can I invite Mr Sitoh Yih Pin if you would like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Yes, Sir, I will keep it very short.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: With that, I ask for leave to withdraw my amendment.
